## What we need & what we did this week
---
|
---
| |
### Volunteers
---
| | Working for a campaign is challenging. Even more so when you are donating your time.
We need to fill some specialty roles as well as have volunteers to accompany us for events, town halls, and canvassers to phone bank and door knock. This is an **ALL HANDS ON DECK** request!
Send an email to [Maria](mailto:volunteer@jonnyutah4congress.com?subject=Interested%20in%20volunteering%20for%20Jonny%20Larsen&body=Full%20name%2C%20phone%2C%20county%20and%20city%20you%20live%20in.%0A%0APlease%20share%20where%20you%20think%20you%20could%20best%20help%20volunteer%20for%20our%20campaign.%20No%20prior%20experience%20is%20needed%20but%20if%20you%20have%20it%2C%20please%20share!), our volunteer coordinator, to find out more.
---
|
---
| |
### Senator Cory Booker
---
| | Senator Cory Booker was in town and met with many Utah Democrats in Salt Lake and in Park City. I was fortunate enough to meet with him and share why we are a competitive district that would benefit from national party help!
Senator Booker shared inspiring stories that touched everyone who attended. What really stood out to me was his message of hope being a muscle. [Check out what he said by clicking here](https://us.list-manage.com/GgGT47yvEoF?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=Q1Eh7dk53KREIMeQsrRAMtWW0ZKdrV1esuV52DzIgQwWayUm9uijxxuOZTU7).
---

| |
### Q3 Meeting In Kane County
---
| | Huge shout out to Kane County Chair Caralee Woods for all the work that she and her amazing team put into hosting the Q3 central committee meeting in Kanab. [See a portion of my speech here](https://us.list-manage.com/TIG8p4Jtrpi?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=hiFHJqlyV6nENDM3COIqRrv5iERtHU5N-RwjcNNk34DhlQwJpcJVjbz0XguQ)
Chair Woods has been a huge supporter of ours for over a year since we first met in May of 2025 at Kane County Convention. I cannot express my gratitude enough for everything that she has done to support me and our campaign.
The food was absolutely amazing and I had a wonderful time. The drive down 89 to view the beautiful red rock is something everyone should experience at least once. If you have not been to Kanab, I highly recommend you go and visit.
---
| |
### Fire devistation continues
---
| | As of Friday, August 14th 2026, the Widemouth 2 fire has been 65% contained. On August 7th we lost two brave men who were instrumental in battling the fire in an unfortunate helicopter crash. Elliott from Porterville, CA and Andersen from Stateline, NV, we honor you for your bravery and dedication to safety of our community. You will not be forgotten, till Valhalla we met brothers. Semper Fi.
Fillmore and the surrounding areas are at high risk for burn scar flooding. As soon as I hear of the next sandbag filling event, I will let everyone know. Let’s show up as a community and help out our neighbors in a time of great need.
---
| |
### Fliers, Door Hangers, and Yard Signs
---
| | We have new fliers, new door hangers, and new yard signs! I had a unique request from a supporter and decided to print a few signs that welcome anyone who might be feeling politically homeless. We have “Republicans For” and “Independents For” yard signs in limited quantities. If you know anyone who is interested in one, invite them to one of our events above so they can come pick one up.
You can find all the canvassing events, door knocking, training, and more at the Utah Democrats mobilize page. Will you step up with a donation to help protect voting rights?
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137262229/640176921/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjI1NjJjOWE4LTNkOTgtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=u-T3smpKfd4Zo9In93vecrpsvWwCp3KLiZ7faHQpo3I=&emci=d6966183-0798-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=2562c9a8-3d98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=8431045)

Peter, It’s been a month since Trump gutted the Election Assistance Commission (EAC) — essentially kneecapping the agency responsible for helping states run elections. name: Roy C.
subject: What’s on my mind tonight
body:
I need you with me before tomorrow’s mid-month deadline.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1123&source=&t=1&akid=2711%2E124072%2E1SiSrq)

---
Peter,
Our mid-month fundraising deadline is tomorrow, so before then, I wanted to personally reach out and share what’s going through my mind.
Republicans are ramping up their attacks against me – personal insults, character smears, baseless TV ads, you name it – and dark-money super PACs are pouring nearly $100 million into this race so far to defeat me.
**They’re spending so much in North Carolina because they know this race could decide U.S. Senate control. However, that’s not the only reason why.**
They know that if I’m elected to the U.S. Senate, I won’t blindly do President Trump’s bidding.
Instead, I’ll hold this Administration accountable when it hurts people, put working families first and do everything I possibly can to make life better for folks in North Carolina and across the country.
**I’m a threat to the GOP’s hold on power, but the only way I can fight back against their attacks is by reaching every fundraising goal from here on out. This race will come down to resources, and donations of $5 or even just a couple bucks matter more than you know.**

Will you chip in what you can to help us meet our $1 million goal, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1123&amount=5&t=8&akid=2711%2E124072%2E1SiSrq)

clean_body: Peter, I'm retiring from Congress, and I honestly expected more. I'm not angry, I'm just disappointed. A few days ago, I sent out the signal calling on every conservative patriot in the nation to help me secure my legacy and rescue this seat from the Democrat vultures. But nothing happened. No cavalry came. As I prepare to step down, it felt like I was left to fight the entire Democratic Party by myself. For a moment, I actually feared for the future of the MAGA movement. But then I remembered, YOU never let us down, Peter. You are the reason for our historic victories, and I know you would never turn your back on this movement, especially now that I am passing the torch to the next generation. I've served as President Trump's Secretary of the Interior and as a SEAL Team 6 Commander. I've given everything to this fight, but now I need to know you'll protect the flame I'm leaving behind. My friend and fellow combat veteran, Aaron Flint, is the only one who can stop the radical left from destroying our agenda once I'm gone. But the truth is, Aaron is hours away from a critical fundraising goal that will determine the fate of this campaign. Democrats have spent millions to destroy me, and they are ready to spend millions more to slander Aaron and flip this seat Blue the moment I walk out the door. you for your support, Peter. name: Mike Rogers
subject: Never did I believe I’d see this in America
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROGERS FOR SENATE
body:
The Cold War is being fought on U.S. soil. Read my personal message.

| |
---
● Personal Message
---
Friend,
---
During my time in **national security** , I learned how to recognize a grave threat to our nation.
---

Fatal Crashes Tied to Foreign-Born Truckers

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FBI FOR FAUCI CELL PHONE RECORDS

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38491&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS9WcmlMR1BNMl9JST91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=a4f1793825b3fdb059464305758b45f29076f7974f091331ee161b6159ee15b2]

The American people should not have to guess about what happened
during the Covid pandemic. They deserve access to the government
records that may help explain how critical decisions were made and how
federal officials exercised their authority.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38456&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWZhdWNpLWNlbGwtcGhvbmVzLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMjgxMi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=87d7a6413d27d9f3312115dde0385a88c2779e453d2b25c8a053714db07da709]
against the U.S. Department of Justice for the contents of Anthony
Fauci’s government-issued cell phones. The phones were provided to
former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
Director Fauci and later reportedly recovered by the FBI (_Judicial
Watch v. U.S. Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38456&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWZhdWNpLWNlbGwtcGhvbmVzLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMjgxMi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=87d7a6413d27d9f3312115dde0385a88c2779e453d2b25c8a053714db07da709]
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38492&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWZhdWNpLWNlbGwtcGhvbmVzLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMjgxMi9dKE5vP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=41bc927e61be6274f05e2e9c8d2bbda5bb6e730d685ddc3ed976c1aa341e7103.
1:26-cv-02812)).

We sued after the FBI failed to comply with a June 2025 FOIA request
for:

> All contents obtained from the government-issued cell phones of
> former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious
> Diseases Anthony Fauci, which were reportedly recovered by the FBI,
> as disclosed to podcaster Joe Rogan by FBI Director Kash Patel in
> the following interview:
> https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38461&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9LeWxlU2VyYXBoaW4vc3RhdHVzLzE5MzEwNTYwMTAzMTMzMjI2OTM/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=de8644dd3d84576b460db8d21233ff73ec5751cc93983484c3ab9fce7ad1ec53

The FBI claimed in October 2025 that the requested records were
located in an investigative file exempt
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=30534&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2ZvaWEtZXhlbXB0aW9ucy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=cc5349e68919db194db68f19a3cfcd91f63649b35fdfaf9d6358cbbcbcc6b458] from
disclosure under FOIA law enforcement exemption 5 U.S.C. §
552(b)(7)(A).

Patel publicly disclosed that the FBI had recovered phones and other
devices that Fauci used during the first Trump administration.

“We just had a great breakthrough this week on Fauci,” Patel told
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38462&F=T&&hash=fbbaf70d124bdd9baef44498eb7ff0eca265b285f506cebf6a8dabca101f0bf8]
Joe Rogan during a June 2025 episode of “The Joe Rogan
Experience.” Patel said investigators had been looking for phones
and devices Fauci used during the first Trump administration and that
“nobody had found it until two days ago.”

Patel cautioned that the devices might not contain everything
investigators were seeking, saying, “Maybe it’s deleted, maybe
it’s not,” but added that the FBI had found the devices and that
the search was “of public importance.”

The FBI’s refusal to release the records comes as congressional
scrutiny of Fauci and the federal government’s handling of the
Covid-19 pandemic intensifies.

On July 29, 2026, Fauci appeared before the Senate Homeland Security
and Governmental Affairs Committee under subpoena. During the hearing,
chaired by Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY), Fauci invoked
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38464&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9ueXBvc3QuY29tLzIwMjYvMDcvMjkvdXMtbmV3cy9hbnRob255LWZhdWNpLXBsZWFkcy10aGUtZmlmdGgtYW1lbmRtZW50LWluLXNlbmF0ZS1oZWFyaW5nLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=957576c32713477174d8417abb623c006f0dd429df6fbfd81a2a12414a1c145a]
the Fifth Amendment 111 times.

On August 6, 2026, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
(HHS) transferred
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38466&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cud3NqLmNvbS9wb2xpdGljcy9wb2xpY3kvYW50aG9ueS1mYXVjaS1jb3ZpZC1waG9uZS1zZW5hdGUtOTZlYmQ4YmU/c3Q9dGNRU2FZJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=00bfd45707fac884a7a014f75773328a094e66f337030916497d981a49326084]
a copy of Fauci’s government-issued iPhone to the Senate Homeland
Security Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, which is chaired by
Sen. Ron Johnson (R-WI).

Also on August 6, the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental
Affairs Committee voted 8-5 to hold Fauci in contempt
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38467&F=T&&hash=b7cd15923c76c9045619fbe6b41105b19145a0948f4186ab94aa8e5f3b655992]
of Congress over his refusal to answer questions about his handling of
the Covid-19 pandemic and his past testimony to Congress regarding
U.S.-funded “gain-of-function” research. The resolution
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38469&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucGF1bC5zZW5hdGUuZ292L3dwLWNvbnRlbnQvdXBsb2Fkcy8yMDI2LzA4L1JPTTI2Mzc2LTEucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=b35a2a6e1c3e87f78ba2f23639b2b86f95ad678212aadca6e0f53c1a95d44fa4]
directs Vice President JD Vance, in his capacity as president of the
Senate, to certify the contempt report to U.S. Attorney for the
District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro for potential prosecution.

Americans have a right to know what the FBI recovered from Fauci’s
government-issued phones and what those records reveal about his
official activities during the Covid pandemic.

Our FOIA lawsuits and investigations have uncovered much of what the
public knows about many Covid-19 controversies:

In May 2026, we filed a post-hearing brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=37876&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbmloLXJveWFsdHktcGF5bWVudC1yZWNvcmRzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=484cb5c01329236e8bd574f1cfca1fa1b5a5c7b0862fb432b2b3b8b7c725b002]
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38471&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbmloLXJveWFsdHktcGF5bWVudC1yZWNvcmRzL11pbj91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=e6417b651df4a29e49e77e8d1f4d6ca5d037ba88e26d876ef7a56bccad0153f3 a FOIA
lawsuit on behalf of Open the Books, urging a federal court to compel
the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to release unredacted records
showing royalty-related payments to government scientists, including

In April 2026, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=37612&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvcmVjb3Jkcy1vbi1jb3ZpZC0xOS1vcmlnaW5zLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=5be05da21b6cda2d61d121bef89dbed283d4b112b709735b6edcd3917f2b75cf] the
Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) for records and
communications of its employees with other government officials
regarding coronaviruses, the Wuhan Institute of Virology (WIV), and
related Covid-19 research.

In March 2026, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=37267&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZ2Fpbi1vZi1mdW5jdGlvbi1yZWNvcmRzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=07852a06db75fab2697d4d57edea19f12964d6721df6440747967bb2e80da9e7] the U.S.
Department of Defense (War Department) for records on funding
proposals submitted to the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
(DARPA) Biological Technologies Office prior to the Covid-19 outbreak.
The Biological Technologies Office was launched
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=37257&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGFycGEubWlsL25ld3MvMjAxNC9iaW9sb2dpY2FsLXRlY2hub2xvZ2llcy1vZmZpY2UtbGF1bmNoP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=9806da4e8a85a1c3565518437d1f2c07d847d84c5175fea05408b80a0b7cb47b]
in 2014.

In June 2025, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=35471&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY292aWQtMTktd3VoYW4tZ2FtZXMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=ca17cbc23d8da4ebd6aba5e254e04af5e1b4522fc4e05a560170f7ee43ae918e] the Defense

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=35428&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9kb3dubG9hZC5taWxpdGFyeW9uZXNvdXJjZS5taWwvMTIwMzgvTU9TL1JlcG9ydHMvMjAxOS1Xb3JsZE1pbGl0YXJ5R2FtZXMtUmVwb3J0RGVjMjAyMi5wZGY/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=cb95a76fe4acb54c147a1d77e461723c7bb4fbdbac41e410e6f8086c2c1ad1ae]

attended the games exhibited Covid-19-like signs and/or symptoms”
during the time surrounding their attendance at the games.

In May 2025, we received records
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=35153&F=T&&hash=77f3aa68fde20d051caad65cd10bb1f197b46b282688222288d3ccdeeb40e8ab]
from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that
revealed its plans to mandate Covid-19 vaccinations for 17 million
health care employees and that only one of 4,682 claims for injuries
and deaths due to Covid-19 “countermeasures” at the time was
compensated.

Records uncovered in 2024 from the Federal Bureau of Investigation
(FBI) through a FOIA request showed an April 2020 email exchange with
several officials in the bureau’s Newark Field Office referring to a
National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) grant to

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84782&L=38494&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZm9yZWlnbmVycy1jb21tZXJjaWFsLWRyaXZlcnMtbGljZW5zZXMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=d921220567666291a1fd7232e3fabc537ea9a0db91d3ad9b3cc5adb9520ae918]

> Foreign nationals unlawfully issued a Commercial Driver’s License
> (CDL) in states run by open border officials killed more than 30
> Americans in 17 fatal crashes last year alone, a disturbing new
> investigation reveals. Among the victims of the senseless highway
> carnage is a 5-year-old girl in California, who was critically
> injured and left with lifelong disabilities after an illegal
> immigrant crashed an 18-wheeler into her family’s vehicle. The
> Golden State leads the pack of offenders, issuing over 128,000
> non-domiciled CDLs between 2022 and 2025 and allowing applicants to
> be tested in Arabic, Chinese, Punjabi, Russian and Spanish with pass
> rates as low as 22% for Arabic speakers and 26% for Punjabi speakers
> compared with 63% for English.
>
> Leftist politicians and bureaucrats in states like California have
> systematically undermined federal CDL standards, a critical public
> safety tool, to license foreign nationals who frequently lack
> English proficiency and valid immigration status to operate
> 80,000-pound big rigs on highways throughout the U.S. The
> consequences have been deadly, according to a probe conducted by the
> Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR), a Washington D.C.
> nonprofit dedicated to studying immigration issues. The group used
> targeted research, public records requests and litigation as well as
> analysis of state Department of Motor Vehicle (DMV) data to conduct

name: Forward Party
subject: In it for the Long Haul
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
We continue to build.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
The Forward Party has been building the infrastructure that serious political change requires. This week, Forward's drivers are proving every step is one we take together for the growth of the movement. More than anything, this is an opportunity to leave a lasting legacy, not through any single campaign or election but by helping build one of the most consequential pieces of civic infrastructure for American politics in a generation.
###
### **This W****ee****k in Texas**
**Mike Collier fought for the movement’s future** On Monday, U.S. District Judge Robert Pitman denied Mike Collier's request for a temporary injunction that would have placed him on the Texas ballot as an independent candidate for Lieutenant Governor. Judge Pitman expressed sympathy for Collier's situation, noting that the burden the law creates is not felt similarly by candidates from the Republican and Democratic parties, but he concluded that it was not clear Collier would have succeeded in getting on the ballot even if Texas had a more moderate requirement. Collier will not be on the November ballot in Texas. That is a loss for the people of Texas who will once again have fewer choices in who to place in elected leadership. This is not the end of the story, however. Not by a long measure. **We highlighted the case in Texas previously and supported Mike in the lawsuit. As a reminder, Texas law requires that an independent candidate for statewide office must collect more than 81,030 valid voter signatures. That alone would be a serious challenge for any campaign, but Texas prohibited independent candidates from signature collection until** **after the primary runoff elections, which gave them only 30 days.** Collier took on Texas's ballot access system, which, we should note, is so burdensome that no independent candidate for statewide office has ever qualified for the ballot in a Texas race with a primary runoff. Mike knew the odds were steep and that the timeline was nearly impossible. The temporary injunction was denied but the constitutional case continues with an expected decision later this year. This ruling does not end the lawsuit. It does not settle the constitutional question. It establishes a legal record and creates precedent for future challenges. Mike Collier did not fight this battle just to get on the ballot in 2026. He fought it to build the case for changes to the ballot in 2028 and beyond. **What We Are Building with Mike Collier and Hundreds of Others Like Him** For our volunteers, donors, Fast Forward readers, and beyond, we want to say directly that our work is real. Our dedication to this country’s democracy is why we have put in the effort all these years. It is why we continue to stand behind the people who see the path to change, and we welcome more every day to join us in building something better. When people talk about a political movement, they usually mean the candidates, the yard signs, the rallies. Those things matter. But the part of a political movement that determines whether it lasts is the part nobody talks about: **the infrastructure that operates underneath it all.** | **Forward has grown state-level teams, now expanding into 41 states with chapters, leaders, volunteers, and the legal standing to participate in the political process as recognized entities**.
---
**We are reaching communities**. The Forward Party's presence in New Mexico, for example, has earned minor party status and is fielding candidates for Magistrate Judge, Public Education Commissioner, State Auditor, and U.S. Senate. New Mexico Forward Party even prevailed on a ballot access dispute before a single court hearing recently. The fact that the filing prompted a county clerk to reverse a disqualification decision illustrates something important about the long game Forward is playing. We are not going away. This is a local story but one that shows the movement is real. Parties that are serious about governing show up in county courthouses and school board races, not just Senate campaigns – and the Forward Party is doing both.
**Real change has never happened fast. It has always happened because people did not stop their pursuit of change.**
---
---

clean_body: We continue to build. | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — The Forward Party has been building the infrastructure that serious political change requires. This week, Forward's drivers are proving every step is one we take together for the growth of the movement. More than anything, this is an opportunity to leave a lasting legacy, not through any single campaign or election but by helping build one of the most consequential pieces of civic infrastructure for American politics in a generation. This Week in Texas Mike Collier fought for the movement’s future On Monday, U.S. District Judge Robert Pitman denied Mike Collier's request for a temporary injunction that would have placed him on the Texas ballot as an independent candidate for Lieutenant Governor. Judge Pitman expressed sympathy for Collier's situation, noting that the burden the law creates is not felt similarly by candidates from the Republican and Democratic parties, but he concluded that it was not clear Collier would have succeeded in getting on the ballot even if Texas had a more moderate requirement. Collier will not be on the November ballot in Texas. That is a loss for the people of Texas who will once again have fewer choices in who to place in elected leadership. This is not the end of the story, however. Not by a long measure. We highlighted the case in Texas previously and supported Mike in the lawsuit. As a reminder, Texas law requires that an independent candidate for statewide office must collect more than 81,030 valid voter signatures. That alone would be a serious challenge for any campaign, but Texas prohibited independent candidates from signature collection until after the primary runoff elections, which gave them only 30 days. Collier took on Texas's ballot access system, which, we should note, is so burdensome that no independent candidate for statewide office has ever qualified for the ballot in a Texas race with a primary runoff. Mike knew the odds were steep and that the timeline was nearly impossible. The temporary injunction was denied but the constitutional case continues with an expected decision later this year. This ruling does not end the lawsuit. It does not settle the constitutional question. It establishes a legal record and creates precedent for future challenges. Mike Collier did not fight this battle just to get on the ballot in 2026. He fought it to build the case for changes to the ballot in 2028 and beyond. Our dedication to this country’s democracy is why we have put in the effort all these years. name: Ken Martin (via DNC HQ)
subject: This was a risky move
body:
---
Derek, I want to tell you about a pretty risky decision that I made last year: For too long, Democratic strategy has been dominated by a boom-and-bust political model. We raise money, build temporary campaign operations late in the cycle, hire short-term organizers, run last-minute advertisements, hold an election, and then dismantle much of the infrastructure we just created. Skilled staff scatter. Field offices close. Local relationships atrophy. Voters may not hear from the party again until the next election, when we return to ask for their votes. Then, every two or four years, we spend enormous sums rebuilding what we allowed to disappear. **When I ran for DNC chair, I knew I wanted to try something different:** Replacing this decades-old campaign model with permanent political infrastructure. We are not choosing between winning now and building for the future. The investments we’re making are designed to do both: Win big this November **_and**_ build a stronger party for the elections that follow. And here’s the thing: **_This new strategy is working.**_ We know that because Democrats have won or overperformed in nearly 90% of key races since Donald Trump took office. Derek, 90% isn’t an accident, it’s hard work paying off. But we can’t take our success in the last year and a half as permission to rest for one single second before November. **I took this calculated risk knowing that we could count on _you_ , our grassroots supporters, to back us.** Which is why I’m writing today to ask: [**Will you chip in $7 to the DNC today? We promise we won’t let your contribution sit in a bank account for months on end, we’ll put it to work right away to power Democrats to victory up and down the ballot, across the country — and build permanent infrastructure to keep that momentum growing far beyond this November.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?refcode=em_20260814_8614_fr&amount=7&refcode2=8614_22930333_E2W8fv&akid=8614%2E22930333%2EE2W8fv) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?express_lane=true&amount=7&refcode=em_20260814_8614_fr&refcode2=8614_22930333_E2W8fv&akid=8614%2E22930333%2EE2W8fv)**

body:
Texas is officially in play for Democrats this year!

| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=week_5_08_14&n=1)
---
Is your household affected by back to school, too? Our small (but mighty!) mostly volunteer team has been working alongside the statewide and county Democratic coordinated campaigns, adding a merch store to our website (launching soon!), setting up Meet & Greets (reply to this email to host one!) and fleshing out GOTV (“Get out the vote”) plans. There are soooo many meetings. But there is also so much encouraging news. Texas is officially in play for Democrats this year! Talarico is surging ahead in the polls against fraudulent, bribery-making, and cheating Ken Paxton.**_
_** And guess what? **We’re going to be listed right under his name on the ballot.** **And thanks to Republicans hubris, this monstrously gerrymandered 27th district is more like a swingable +6 than a +15.** So when Democrats go to the polls this year, they are going to have back-to-back hard working teachers to vote for. But it goes beyond Democrats. We’re growing the coalition here in TX-27 to include: 🚢 Veterans who are watching sailors deployed in the Middle East jump overboard because _the conditions on the ships are so horrific._ 🏥 Parents who lost health insurance and are now desperately _praying their kids don’t get sick._ 💰 Small business owners who might have to close and let go of their employees because _life has gotten so d*mn expensive for everyone._ The money you invest in this race helps Democratic candidates up and down the entire ballot, from Talarico to our local council member.
---
**_This Upcoming Week at a Glance_** _Sunday, August 16th_ | Sign up for upcoming events like our [South Austin Meet & Greet](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/meet_greet_shady_hollow?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=week_5_08_14&n=2). Not in Austin, but have friends or family in Austin? Please share! **_Some of Last Week’s Highlights_**

And we need resources to push us past the finish line. If you have ever thought about donating, the time is NOW.** Let’s make history together to flip Texas.

I’ve spent a lot of time ever since I awoke from my coma reflecting on the big picture of what my trial in Arizona is really all about.

Seizing my assets.
Forcing me to the point of bankruptcy._

**And now, a vengeful Democrat Attorney General making me stand in a rigged trial for bogus state-level crimes, because she knows that not even the most powerful man on the face of the planet – President Trump – can save me with a _federal_ pardon in _state_ court.**

The lunatic Left’s desire to DESTROY yours truly knows no bounds.

But what I’ve come to realize ever since I came so close to death was that the pursuit of truth, freedom, and justice are worth infinitely more than any earthly possession.
---
**They can strip me of all I’m worth – _all I’ll ever be worth_ – but what I _REFUSE_ to surrender to the Democrats and their Deep State thugs is my LEGACY!**

And __that__ is what my final trial is truly all about, Friend.
---
**I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.”**
---
"__For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?_ " (Mark 8:36)_
---
You see, this FINAL BATTLE for my freedom is about ensuring this injustice can _NEVER_ _AGAIN_ happen to another innocent patriot all for standing by what he knows to be right and true.
---
I pray to God that will be my legacy when we win this trial.
---
But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: _good and honest Americans like _YOU__.
---
Friend, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it.
---
_**But if you can help, I’m going to need the best defense I can get to defeat this radical Democrat Attorney General who is hell-bent on locking me up for the rest of my life.**_

subject: Update on the Campaign, Ways to Get Involved, & Upcoming Events
body:
Only 80 days until Election Day
| | | | |
---
| We've had a busy several weeks on the campaign trail! As we continue to approach Election Day, I want to give a brief update on the campaign, including a list of upcoming events and ways you can get involved.
Check it out below!
---
| An Update on the Trail
---
| |
---
Last week after our campaign breakfast at The Rose (more on that below), I was honored to participate on a panel at the Georgia Chamber of Commerce's annual Congressional Luncheon in Athens, where more than 2,500 people from across the state gathered here in the 10th District.
Earlier in the week, I toured Caterpillar's Athens plant and recently visited Jackson EMC headquarters. I also attended the groundbreaking for St. Mary's new facility at Lake Oconee, and we've been making many other stops across the district in between. One of the most meaningful moments was spending time with the young leaders at Frontline Policy. I was especially honored when they took time to pray over our team. I'm truly thankful for the next generation of young people who are stepping up, getting involved, and committed to making a difference.
We are now just about eight weeks away from early voting, and there is no slowing down. Over the coming weeks, I'll be continuing to travel across the district--meeting folks, attending events, and listening to the priorities that matter most to the people I'm running to represent. Our team is hitting the ground hard, too. We're knocking on doors, recruiting new volunteers, and building the grassroots organization we'll need for the final stretch.
There is plenty of work ahead, but I'm encouraged by the momentum we're building and the growing number of people joining our team. With 80 days until Election Day, our focus is simple: keep showing up, keep working hard, and keep building a strong organization across all 20 counties as we head toward early voting and Election Day.
---

| Breakfast at the Rose
---
| We had a PACKED house at the Rose Downtown in Athens for our breakfast fundraiser last week! Thank you to everyone who joined us for this great event. I'm especially grateful to the many statewide and local elected officials and candidates who attended, along with nearly 150 friends and supporters. We had a great conversation about the stakes in November and the importance of electing conservatives up and down the ballot.

Earlier in the week, I toured Caterpillar's Athens plant and recently visited Jackson EMC headquarters. I also attended the groundbreaking for St. Mary's new facility at Lake Oconee, and we've been making many other stops across the district in between. One of the most meaningful moments was spending time with the young leaders at Frontline Policy. I was especially honored when they took time to pray over our team. I'm truly thankful for the next generation of young people who are stepping up, getting involved, and committed to making a difference. We are now just about eight weeks away from early voting, and there is no slowing down. Over the coming weeks, I'll be continuing to travel across the district--meeting folks, attending events, and listening to the priorities that matter most to the people I'm running to represent. Our team is hitting the ground hard, too. We're knocking on doors, recruiting new volunteers, and building the grassroots organization we'll need for the final stretch. There is plenty of work ahead, but I'm encouraged by the momentum we're building and the growing number of people joining our team. With 80 days until Election Day, our focus is simple: keep showing up, keep working hard, and keep building a strong organization across all 20 counties as we head toward early voting and Election Day. | | | | | | | | | | | Breakfast at the Rose | We had a PACKED house at the Rose Downtown in Athens for our breakfast fundraiser last week! Thank you to everyone who joined us for this great event. I'm especially grateful to the many statewide and local elected officials and candidates who attended, along with nearly 150 friends and supporters. We had a great conversation about the stakes in November and the importance of electing conservatives up and down the ballot. If you missed it, we'd love to have you join us for our General Election Kickoff in Athens on August 31st - == | | | | | | | | | | | | | Less than 3 Months Until Election Day 3 Ways to Get Involved: 1. ## Election Night Watch Party
Tuesday, August 18th at 7 pm - Midnight!
Join Team Marialana Kinter and Central Florida supporters of Angie Nixon for an Election Night Watch Party on Tuesday, August 18th at 7:00 PM at the Sanford Women's Club, 309 S. Oak Ave, Sanford, FL 32771, following a full day of Election Day phone banking and canvassing from 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM. We'll come together to celebrate the work we've done, watch the results come in, and recognize the grassroots volunteers and organizations that made this campaign possible. The evening will feature food, champagne, a DJ, live bands, and speakers from organizations that have endorsed and supported our movement. Angie Nixon will be celebrating in her hometown of Jacksonville, but her Central Florida supporters will be joining Team Kinter for the evening. Both campaigns are fighting for Medicare for All, universal childcare, expanding Social Security and veterans benefits, and getting corporate money and special interests out of our political system. All ages are welcome, but you must be 21 or older to drink and IDs will be checked at the bar. Come spend Election Day with us, make calls, knock doors, connect with voters, and then join us that evening as we watch the results together.

body:
Insulin costs. Alzheimer's research. Maine values. Will you stand with me?

| [](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine._Lz9yZWN1cnJpbmc9dHJ1ZSZhbW91bnQ9NTAmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwODE1X0VSLVo3LjExMDExN190MTk4OTAwMy0xMTQyJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDgxNV9FUi1aNy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5ODkwMDMtMTE0MiJ9/b3HPsL7nFb2YGFfWeGSydg)

Peter,I grew up in Aroostook County, Maine - as far north as you can go and still be in the continuous United States. It's a place where people work with their hands, look out for their neighbors, and don't expect anyone to hand them anything.That's the Maine I carry with me every single day in Washington.It's why, when I became Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, one of the most powerful posts in the entire Senate, I didn't forget where I came from. I use that gavel to fight for the things that actually matter to families like the ones I grew up with:
---
* Capping the cost of insulin so no Mainer living with diabetes has to choose between medication and groceries.
* Fighting for real funding for Alzheimer's research, because I've seen what this disease does to families, and I refuse to look away.
* Delivering for our veterans, our farmers, our fishermen, and our small towns that Washington so often forgets.

---
I didn't take the easy path to get here, and I'm not taking the easy path now. But I can't do this alone.Maine gave me everything. Now I need you to stand up for Maine.[Can I count on you to please chip in today and help me keep fighting for the people who raised me?](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine._Lz9yZWN1cnJpbmc9dHJ1ZSZhbW91bnQ9NTAmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwODE1X0VSLVo3LjExMDExN190MTk4OTAwMy0xMTQyJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDgxNV9FUi1aNy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5ODkwMDMtMTE0MiJ9/cihUbdNIS3rzwbtMyp6XvA)

| Peter,
On April 29th, 2026, the Supreme Court issued their infamous Callais v. Louisiana verdict -- the single greatest rollback of civil rights in America since the darkest days of Jim Crow.
In their majority opinion, the court ruled to gut the Voting Rights Act of key protections for minority voters and restore Jim Crow style gerrymandering across the deep south.
Immediately Louisiana's far-right Governor sprung into action and declared a 'state of emergency' cancelling our elections and giving the Louisiana state legislature time to successfully erase one of our only Black majority districts.
In response, we reached out to Democrats across the nation with an urgent call for support. They answered. We raised nearly $2,000,000 in less than two weeks. name: Roy Cooper
subject: Not an easy decision
body:
This race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are too high.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1124&source=&t=1&akid=2698%2E124072%2EPoo6lF)
| | | |
---
Peter, deciding to run for this U.S. Senate seat wasn’t easy.
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. That’s why I was so humbled when North Carolinians twice elected me to be their Governor.
**But this Senate race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
I entered this race to fight for people like you, who’ve put your trust in me – and I have full faith that together, we can win. But tonight, we’re facing a crucial test of our grassroots movement’s strength:
At 11:59 p.m., our mid-month deadline will come to a close. [**_So with time running out to reach our ambitious $1 million goal, I’m personally asking you to help out by making your first $5 donation, right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1124&amount=5&t=8&akid=2698%2E124072%2EPoo6lF)
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1124&amount=5&t=9&akid=2698%2E124072%2EPoo6lF)
---
I’m running because our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked Republican power in Washington. The attacks on health care, on democratic values and even on Americans – **they have to stop.**
Our leaders should be focusing on strengthening our communities by investing in public schools, securing health care access and prioritizing hardworking folks over the wealthiest few. That’s what I strove to do in North Carolina – and by the end of my time in office, we added thousands of jobs by expanding the clean energy economy, gave public school teachers statewide a much-needed raise, expanded Medicaid and more.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8315%2E582294%2EDhSpvQ)
This is not the email I wanted to send.
We’ve been telling you that New Hampshire is a top target for national Republicans. They’re pouring millions of dollars into our state to flood the airwaves and flip this seat red.
Now new polls have our opponent just one point away from us — in the margin of error. A virtual tie.
And we're _still_ being outspent 3-to-1.
We won’t be able to match them dollar for dollar, **but we can show them that New Hampshire is not for sale.**
**[Will you step up for the first time and donate to our campaign? Every dollar goes toward reaching more voters and supporting our volunteer-powered campaign.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260815_1.h8MCuV&refcode=em20260815-1&t=2&akid=8315%2E582294%2EDhSpvQ)**

Peter,
The unthinkable is happening before our very eyes.
For years Nebraska's 1st Congressional District, currently represented by ultra-MAGA extremist Congressman Mike Flood (R-NE), has been written off and labeled unwinnable for Democrats. As of Wednesday, this is no longer the case.
In a seismic shift, the DCCC, the campaign arm for House Democrats, just announced that Nebraska's 1st Congressional District is now part of their "districts in play," a program for districts seen as highly competitive.
---
| [](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001htV_zA2eNSyvk_B6_zbpUJNKXzSTE6XzaonRJW2bc-8QX5aSCu4mbk3WPIE6wFUXffN7p38BXkaS6nxAsR_bWbkJ8vrcnQRt2uc0LiULbcQSpYyKFVqEE5etA8Pg5MIgCTL7r5Gi7mEdO_GzRy-5rbFj4TTECexdB6LL0Mkgu7vBx1rdWvL_NoI-LGLWeoDKpBBzY6fvyf96E43ELAE3n9UZcGjCCGg6WEgx9aAuG_E=&c=Zq3Rs2gE9SXENOGnNNfh7aSX_Tmie6XOGgxLrsUQ6pSVAp3BxBH01A==&ch=nBZVaGP32gCoLQxZtChyyPaFu6y5eI9xfaKJqIqlU51v6IEWZe_xtg==)
---
Congressman Flood is deeply vulnerable. Testament to this is the uproar and backlash Flood faces anytime he steps out in public.
At every single town hall he's hosted, constituents show up en masse to absolutely obliterate him.
In many cases 400+ constituents will show up to heckle, boo, and ask cutting questions that expose his contempt for working Nebraskans.
But this district's competitiveness stems from more than just Flood's unpopularity. The reason why this race is in play is because of the caliber of his Democratic opponent:
Chris Backemeyer, a 21-year career civil servant with the US State Department, who saw firsthand the impact of MAGA's efforts to undermine the federal workforce.
A year ago this race, and a state like Nebraska for that matter, were considered unwinnable. Yet thanks to the hard work of Democrats across Nebraska and across the nation -- no red district or red state is out of reach for us. When we organize everywhere we can win anywhere.
The blue wave has arrived and we need your support to ensure it WASHES across Nebraska. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

clean_body: I received a heartbreaking message from Tyler Tew, a J6 patriot in desperate need of help, and wanted to pass it along. Peter, I received a heartbreaking message from Tyler Tew, a J6 patriot in desperate need of help, and wanted to pass it along. Tyler was a commercial pilot for 14 years... until Joe Biden 's TSA revoked his commercial pilot's license for "suspicion of terrorism" without even being charged with a crime. As a result of his lost pilot's salary, Tyler's family business is now in bankruptcy, and he, his wife, and their four kids are in desperate need of your support. I promised Tyler Stand in the Gap could help raise the funds he needs to get his company back on track, and Peter, Tyler's message absolutely broke my heart, and I'd like you to read it if you have a moment: My name is Tyler Tew. I was a commercial airline pilot for 14 years. I flew for SkyWest as a Captain and then Allegiant. I graduated from Utah State with an aviation degree and built my entire life around flying. I went to Washington on January 6 after being invited by friends. After President Trump's speech, I went to the Capitol. What I saw with my own eyes did not match what the news reported. On March 26, 2021, the TSA revoked my commercial pilot 's license for "suspicion of terrorism" and being a threat to the national airspace -- before I was ever charged with a crime and before any FBI interview.I spent $40,000 in legal fees. In June 2021, Allegiant fired me. Without my W-2 income, I could no longer sustain the construction company my wife and I owned. It is now in bankruptcy. We have four children. I now work 6-7 days a week in construction just to survive. I'm hoping Stand in the Gap can help us raise $25,000 to stabilize our family and our company during this bankruptcy and help us recover from the financial destruction caused by the sudden end of my aviation career. We have nowhere else to turn. Thank you for anything you can do. -- Tyler Tew Tyler's story is why we started our Fund Their Futures fundraising program, Peter. President Trump's pardons gave these patriots back their freedom... but that did NOT give them their lives, careers, businesses, or homes back. Tyler did everything right for decades... building a wonderful career, a small business, and a loving family. It all ended WITHOUT due process ... simply because the Far-Left wanted to punish him for supporting President Trump. Your gift today will give Tyler and his family breathing room. It'll help stabilize their company and help them keep a roof over their heads. Stand with the Gap exists specifically for moments like this... to when the legal fight is over, but the fight to survive has just begun. Too often, Stand in the Gap is the for the men and women who faced political persecution and financial ruin after January 6. We exist to share the burden and make it lighter ... and your generosity is quite literally the difference between families like Tyler's losing everything. That's why I hope you'll step forward, Peter. Even just a few dollars could make a critical difference. Thank you so much for helping them out. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: We can overcome this map

body:
The map might be rigged but the fight isn’t over.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2992%2E4032634%2EbYKaXj)
---
Did you know Virginia is heading into the midterm elections with a congressional map that gives Republicans an advantage? Here's why: Back in May, the Supreme Court of Virginia overturned Virginia's redistricting referendum, nullifying the election results — and the votes of more than 3,000,000 voters. So Virginians are stuck with a map designed to help Republicans win. **But the good news? Last week, Virginia Democrats nominated three strong candidates: Tom Perriello, Shannon Taylor, and Elaine Luria.** And here's what matters: winning these three races puts us one step closer to taking back our power in Congress. And once we have our majorities back, we can block Trump's far-right judges, stop Republicans from rubber-stamping whatever he wants, and make Trump actually follow the law. [**That’s why overcoming Republicans’ redistricting scheme matters. And it's why I’m asking you to split a contribution between our movement and Tim, Shannon, and Elaine’s campaigns. Every dollar helps these candidates reach voters, overcome a Republican-friendly map, and fight for the seats that could put us closer to taking back our majorities.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3746?t=8&akid=2992%2E4032634%2EbYKaXj)

name: Alex Vindman
subject: Up early
body:
I’m sending this from my car

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260815-1&refcode2=1062_3892029_OEhUry&akid=1062%2E3892029%2EOEhUry)
---
Good morning, Peter! Alex Vindman here. I’m getting ready for a rally in Miami, but wanted to send you a quick note beforehand. (Excuse any typos, I’m typing this in the car.)
Let me be honest: I’m not a career politician. If you told me while I was serving in Iraq that I would be running for office one day, I would’ve called you insane.
But there’s one thing that connects it all: Service.
I’ve dedicated my life to service and sacrifice. I spent 21 years in the Army under presidents of both parties. And even though Donald Trump ended my military career for speaking the truth, he couldn’t undercut my loyalty to our country.
America is in a moment of peril. We need citizens to step up and fight back for the soul of this country before it’s too late. That’s why I’m running for the U.S. Senate against Trump’s most loyal henchmen, Ashley Moody — someone who voted with him 100% of the time last year.
I wouldn’t be running for Senate if I didn’t believe deep down that we could win. But I can’t do it without you: National Republicans are spending big to hammer me in attack ads. The only way we can flip this seat is with an overwhelming amount of grassroots support right now.
Peter, can I count on you to donate $10 to my campaign? Let’s show Trump and the billionaires that we have the grassroots power to win this Senate seat and deliver a Democratic Senate majority in November.

We just fought through the most expensive Democratic Senate primary in Michigan history — and won it without taking a single dollar from corporate PACs.
I’ll be honest, winning the primary took everything this campaign had.
Here's something nobody tells you on election night: **winning doesn't refill a bank account. The primary basically drained ours at the exact moment the _real fight_ started.**
Meanwhile, our Republican opponent Mike Rogers has $51 million in Super PAC money and a whole MAGA mega-donor network ready to spend whatever it takes to flip Michigan red.

subject: Congress looked at me like I had two heads
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Burchett for Congress

Hey Peter, Tim Burchett here.
I’ve got a reputation in Congress for asking questions folks in Washington would rather dodge.
Not the kind that gets you on TV. Not the kind that makes the evening news.
Questions like:
"Where exactly did that $40 billion go?"
"Why does this bill have 3,000 pages if there are only 100 important things in it?"
"Can someone explain to me why we keep funding programs that don't work?"
My colleagues look at me like I've got two heads sometimes. I don't care.
[Because those are YOUR questions.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-j_GtTed6Wv2WPpb4TBeOw)
And if you want a Congressman to sit quietly and clap like a trained seal while they burn through your money, then y’all definitely picked the wrong fella.
Problem is, the people getting rich off this mess would love to send me packing.
They’ve got lobbyists, PAC cash, and enough slick-haired consultants to fill a Nashville hotel ballroom.
I’ve got grassroots patriots like you, Peter.
[And if you’re still with me, rush a small donation and help me keep asking the questions nobody else will:](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-wxJwU2fqVWoDNMq7g)

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Spare us the Data Center Hypocrisy
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/july4th-12854439?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
There are certain modern hypocrisies I notice all the time.

People who complain about capitalism while living in the wealthiest capitalist countries on earth. Progressive activists in America who lament the lack of respect for individual freedom — seemingly unaware of how much of the rest of the world actually lives. People who use a smartphone to post about how much they hate Big Tech.

The newest one is those who complain about data centers while enjoying the extraordinary technology that data centers make possible.

Every industrial advance has needed something to power it. The first — textiles — ran on water wheels, and then on steam engines. The second, of iron and steel, depended on coal. We are only in the foothills of an even greater transformation, and what makes this one possible is electricity and data centers.

I get the argument that you might not want a data center literally next door. That is a fair thing for a neighbor to say. But Mississippi has just under three million people spread across nearly 47,000 square miles. I think we can manage to build where we need to without blotting out the sunshine or using all the water.

Irrigation accounts for about two-thirds of all the water Mississippi uses — our farmers consume vastly more than any data center will. And Mississippi gets almost 56 inches of rain a year. There is more than enough for every farmer and every data center we could possibly build. Amazon's Canton facility already uses outside air for cooling 91 percent of the year, and from 2027 will run its cooling entirely on recycled wastewater.

Nor do data centers pollute. There are no billowing smokestacks of the kind that marked earlier industrial advances. What there is, is tax revenue.
---
|
---
**_Data centers – not much pollution_**
| The numbers in Madison County are worth reading twice. Amazon's data centers there are projected to deliver around $14 million to the community in 2027, rising to roughly $145 million a year by 2033 — including $38 million a year for Madison County schools, $38 million for Canton schools, and $3 million a year for Hinds Community College. Amazon's total commitment across Mississippi now stands at $25 billion.

Which makes what is happening in local government all the more striking.

In July, the City of Jackson voted 5–2 for a six-month moratorium on data centers. Jackson sits in Hinds County — a part of our state that could do more with additional tax revenue than almost anywhere else. And Hinds County is one part of the state where Amazon is already investing: a billion dollars, at Clinton, a few miles down the road.

In Olive Branch, Mayor Ken Adams told the Board of Aldermen this month that the city has spent four months drafting what he described as "a very restrictive" data center ordinance.

There are good arguments in some cases against a data center in a particular neighborhood, and most of these decisions properly belong to local people. But overall, Mississippi should be very pro data center — and not just because of the tax revenue stream they could bring.

AI is going to be a force for good. Sure, like the printing press or the personal computer, it will allow bad people to do bad things. But overall it will make the world a better place. Already, AI is allowing productive people to do far more.

Every new technology has been said to take jobs. In England, Ned Ludd's followers smashed the stocking frames they feared would take theirs. They were wrong. The same warning has since been issued about the tractor, the spreadsheet, the ATM and the shipping container.

In fact the opposite happens. There have never been more jobs in the United States than there are today — close to 159 million Americans on payrolls last month. The real challenge for America's leaders is not a shortage of work. It is a shortage of good employees.

One of the most basic laws of economics is that as the price of something goes down, people buy more of it. Far from producing mass unemployment among lawyers and doctors, AI will lower the cost of legal and medical advice — and we will ask for a great deal more of both. The model for delivering professional advice might change. The number of folk earning a living from the provision of it will grow.

When Matt Ridley came to speak for us in Jackson in March, he called this the Jevons paradox. So who was Jevons?

William Stanley Jevons was an English economist, and one of the first to insist that economics be done with numbers rather than assertions. In 1865 he published The Coal Question, in which he pointed out something that ought to have been impossible. James Watt's steam engine burned far less coal than the engines it replaced. Everyone therefore assumed that Britain would burn less coal. Britain burned vastly more. Because Watt had made steam power cheap, mill owners and mine owners and shipbuilders put engines everywhere, and national coal consumption soared. "It is a confusion of ideas," Jevons wrote, "to suppose that the economical use of fuel is equivalent to diminished consumption. The very contrary is the truth."

We should welcome data centers, glory in the AI revolution underway, and be at the forefront of it.
---

Easy to say when you’re the richest man on the planet.

Someday, AI might make guaranteed income possible — whether it’s $500 a month or $4,000. But that could be 20 years away.

So while you wait for AI to deliver your government check — which may be 20 years from now — I want to show you [something that actually exists today.](https://links.notify.powerfieldnotes.com/u/click?_t=e11a13a19fbf4d1ab3d90eea26ea896f&_m=0fba6c2d78964c2bad3aaa98493773bd&_e=SP-eiZJMy45MRsBA2bytk_MoouT2O4DdK7OZdrt3V9Qc_61h2DuUr8HW_E3l_VnX7LltbesMjyIsRzXOLYcUNuJyKkFpTuDbqI6X8JVmIULdoFseDHKIj4rK5j0s7ETzFo3OO2A7BD-T8DYB4Fbj1VCKfO_gcqxQZm0y89yTJ5ccrCE19KTZrE80WG9RhcMoNrEd0RtDO_XPmxxzJyglDR63XiZf3eKjk-Uw0KA07GqpMnJHlMQO85KlC79Yzpey8xf-EJnvpYRWPuH6uyJsmSFeZkwzM7PMXkPijUtPmA9gsnabVz20Z5Yp4Tf26i6wHEnWqXoUEhnaVj0DHQ87S8HwbT9EeP27L-1pNpC_4d-_8Y4bPCtwbolk2an8LqlJFTY4VY55KYSJ8_wQ_LntGTNiOohmXlyaCRxgnrG690POaFoCVh2q_8nvF-BS1pSCuNoiLDmxcBfpA5t1JfTQylF_4hHlQarGkcQKiAB4z4Q%3D)

| | **The July Producer Price Index Came in Flat, Held Down by a 5.7% Drop in Fuel Prices. Two Days After the CPI Eased to 3.4%, the Disinflation Is Confirmed — but It, Too, Ended Before $88 Brent.**
---
| | The second inflation reading of the week reinforced the first: the July Producer Price Index came in flat for the month, held down by a sharp drop in fuel prices. **Producer fuel prices fell about 5.7% in July after sharp increases through the early part of the year driven largely by the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.** Coming two days after the July CPI eased to 3.4%, the flat PPI confirms the disinflation was real and broad-based — extending from the prices consumers pay to the prices producers charge.
---
| | For your portfolio, the PPI matters as a forward-looking complement to the CPI because it measures inflation earlier in the supply chain — the costs producers face before passing them to consumers. A flat PPI driven by falling fuel suggests the pipeline pressure on future consumer prices eased in July. **But the same caveat that applied to the CPI applies with even greater force: July’s fuel decline is backward-looking, capturing a month when average energy prices were still falling — before this week’s Brent surge toward $88 and the nearly 5% weekly gain.** For the American investor at or near retirement, the two-report confirmation — CPI Wednesday, PPI today — solidifies the near-term case for a September Fed hold, supporting the roughly 55% hold probability the market has priced. But both readings reflect a July already in the rearview mirror. Welcome the clean picture, let it support the near-term hold, but don’t extrapolate it: the producer pipeline that cooled in July will reflect $88 Brent when the August numbers arrive.

Peter,

Growing up in St. Louis as the son of a police officer and county civil servant, I learned early on what it meant to work hard and look out for the people around you.

I went to Hazelwood East, worked multiple jobs to put myself through college, and eventually came home to serve this community. St. Louis made me who I am, **and every single day I'm in Congress, I remember exactly who sent me there and who I'm fighting for.**

I'm fighting for families watching their grocery bills climb, seniors worried about the cost of their prescriptions, and workers who deserve good-paying jobs and a fair shot — all while standing up to a Trump administration and MAGA Republicans threatening our rights, our democracy, and the communities we're supposed to serve.

I've learned that real change doesn't happen by sitting on the sidelines; it happens when people show up, do the work, and keep going. body:
Over the safety and security of our community
| | | | Hi Friend,
When asked directly about his party's direction, Suhas didn't push back on the socialist wing taking hold of the Democratic Party, he embraced it, saying his caucus is "united more than people think" because it includes DSA members alongside moderates. That's the same DSA that has pushed to abolish the police and abolish prisons in cities across this country. **When given the chance to draw a clear line, Suhas chose common ground with the DSA instead.**
---
|
---
|
---
**I will never put VA-10's safety and way of life at risk to keep peace within my own party.** I will always stand with law enforcement, defend the Constitutional rights of every citizen, and fight for a government that lives within its means instead of chasing radical ideas that have failed everywhere they've been tried. That's not a slogan for me, it's the same principle I built thirty years of service around.
This race is going to be close. Suhas may have the resources of the national Democratic machine behind him, but I have VA-10 families who refuse to let DSA ideology take root in this district.
**If you're one of them, I need your help today to keep fighting, unseat Suhas, and make sure the DSA ideology _never_ gets a foothold in VA-10.**

God Bless, Dave Beckwith

Kroger, America's largest traditional grocery chain, has increasingly blurred the line between supermarket and surveillance firm. A 2025 investigation by Consumer Reports found that the company monetizes customer data on an unprecedented scale, while its adoption of electronic shelf labels has stoked fears of algorithmic "surge pricing" for everyday food.
Through its loyalty program, Kroger tracks roughly 63 million households, capturing not only what they buy, but when they shop, how they pay, and what they browse online. The grocer then deploys sophisticated analytics to build detailed shopper profiles--estimating income, brand preferences, and even willingness to pay premium prices. This data fuels Kroger's "precision marketing" division, which sells aggregated and individualized insights to third-party advertisers and brands. According to Consumer Reports, this arm generated approximately $527 million in a single year. Packaged with other ancillary ventures under the banner of "alternative profit," data-driven sales now account for more than 35 percent of Kroger's net income--making surveillance nearly as lucrative as selling produce and pantry staples.
The company insists the practice is legal and disclosed in its privacy policy, which loyalty members must accept to unlock discounts. However, critics note that few shoppers understand the depth of profiling involved. Consumer Reports obtained sample profiles showing Kroger's income estimates could be wildly inaccurate, raising questions about fairness and transparency. For consumers, the real price of a digital coupon may be the quiet commodification of their grocery habits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bcb3da3b-91f7-4a8a-97e8-7c3184ba93a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Parallel to its data business, Kroger is accelerating a technological overhaul of store pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs)--digital tags that replace paper price cards--are being rolled out across its banners, including Fred Meyer, Ralphs, and Harris Teeter. The technology allows prices to be updated remotely and instantaneously, ostensibly to improve operational efficiency and reduce labor costs. But lawmakers warn the same infrastructure enables dynamic pricing, in which costs fluctuate based on demand, weather, time of day, or other transient factors.
In an August 2024 letter to then-CEO Rodney McMullen, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Bob Casey cautioned that Kroger's partnership with AI firm IntelligenceNode--plus its history of marketplace analytics--suggests the grocer could abuse digital tags to "squeeze consumers" by raising prices during peak demand. Analysts have warned that widespread dynamic pricing could make groceries "priced like airline tickets," introducing volatility into household budgets already strained by inflation. Grocery Dive reported that Kroger came under direct fire for the labels, with critics noting food spending as a share of income is already at a 30-year high.
Defenders of ESL technology argue there is no imminent plan for airline-style surge pricing, and that the tags primarily streamline promotions and inventory management. Still, the convergence of granular surveillance and instantaneous price adjustment creates a troubling prospect: a retailer that knows exactly how much each household will pay and can change the tag in seconds.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3913671f-c166-4541-8702-d67d69b1e542?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
During natural disasters like hurricanes and wildfires, price gouging predictably surges as merchants and opportunistic resellers inflate the cost of gasoline, bottled water, generators, and lodging--often exploiting legal ambiguity or localized shortages before enforcement catches up. The COVID-19 pandemic mirrored this dynamic on a national scale when panic buying emptied shelves of toilet paper, disinfectants, and masks, prompting some retailers and third-party sellers to impose steep markups that outpaced any plausible supply-chain cost increase. While state-level consumer-protection laws and emergency declarations typically prohibit excessive price hikes during crises, the fine line between legitimate scarcity pricing and predatory gouging often blurs, leaving regulators scrambling to distinguish profiteering from the inflationary pressure of disrupted logistics and consumer hysteria.
For shoppers, the lesson is stark. The loyalty card that saves a dollar on cereal may also train a model that sells your profile to the highest bidder, while the digital tag beneath the box could rewrite the price the moment demand spikes. Kroger's transformation reflects a broader retail trend--one where your data is the product and the shelf edge is the new frontier of algorithmic commerce.
