## Texas Schools Get A-F Report Cards
The Texas Education Agency [released A-F accountability grades](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDESmzAQRU8jOjHSgkEUKtLQOW1KZpEWo7FAHmkD9u0zeJITpP6z-_97v-7THUMM--MnbmT5vaRpp7NEYqY8FbemFMsjoyefisN8hn2nvE2goJPKSH2b0HE4aGqx8nZWftAVWd2brh-GpoFqtQQwL60ZqOmcBlTQK-0br2c3K6NmXwV7vVNG33SjzE3VTad6MkM7aA04t160inzglGteiemNZYmfdFCuXdqqaFfmVxHNDwGjgPE8z_pZkK9QwHjxCBi_ZwLGq0rAqIyAUbf_AvkXVWZyFA6SKBeJzqXfO-McYuCP_GooEovcUibpQ-EcHBe5phdJThKPFLxkfNK17SqrsvWvM8QYSteLVj02DPE7mv9X9mHhTwAAAP__82-V5Q) Friday for public schools and districts statewide, with 24% of campuses earning an A and 14% receiving a D or F. ## Mangione Pleads Guilty in CEO Killing
Luigi Mangione [pleaded guilty](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGunTAQRVdjOtB4bMAULtK4-2lTonkwBkcGI-P3ELuPSJQV_Gqa0bn33F9f4xeFGPblJ21si0_jztcZuRTO40b7EtLOyzvEch-RaffxyHyOCNjVYGrZjjSV8OFRUzVbz4ysKrayN10_DBp0tVpSulW67fxLt9RNhqBXvjP-RXI2_ctUwT48MLKVSgKoRtLEKFszgZetAik08BxKys3vFPayso93-nBuprRV0a6lHKdQPwQ6ge66ruZ9Ukkz3c-DQHeWlG-B7nF7DpWQdoHuiRXowAh0Ugt08R2WUP_3rv-J155nzhTraaW88EMYJA6gBgToBboq2_m4Qozh7HqhYdkoxL_dyjcn_Vj8EwAA___PUYk6) Friday to two federal stalking charges in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, telling the court, _"I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan, and he died."_ Each charge carries a maximum of life in prison. Mangione, 28, admitted he [posed as an investor](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u4yAQBeCnwR3RMPgHFxTbuMu2W1rEHuxZYbCAJMrbr7xX9wlufaRz9J0_9_nuOHDcfruDbPVpjvQugWqlPB8ubpwibU8O9XMGctGHM1OZEbCXYKTqZrdUftHcuma1nghJN2TVYPphHFtom92O3QON6R_O9y3q1qAB8EZR58w6dKtu2F59YFSntALQN-UWQtWZBbzqNCjRAq1cU779TRzrTj580ovybUlHE-xe61mE_iVwEjjVnXYO4coETns66CIJnHrAcdQgw5M3lt84ebnWIr-Q0tNK2QW5uELykdlFWfd0nCVFgVOT7Xq-OQQu_SBa2A7H_5ea-sPzXhb_BQAA__9RYYTb) and emailed UnitedHealthcare to confirm Thompson's location before the fatal shooting outside a Manhattan hotel. He said he 3D printed the gun and attached a silencer. His defense team immediately filed a [double jeopardy motion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uxCAQBeDT4I4V4J_FBUUauk2b0po1gz0JBsvgXe3tIxLlBKlH8_S-93GbbkCB4vIOG5ri0xTxmQOWgse0QVwoRVxOCuW1B4Tow35gnpRQAxeay36CudADpw4aZzyiwrZBI696uI5jJ7pmNYDD0IMDrzs5w6il72fv3X10rWr1ODZkap7QspetFKK9SJhRyV7Pwsu-FZJ1Ah2VdFw-E8Wyog-v9MDjMqetCWYtZc-sfWPKMmXja0-51BNTtgYzZYVmysqOKXtmXoVM2XDSQvzPyCvPZf5r5RT5F4U6DE-en5EKuhUhlHWGA_k95czvB0HkZU3bnlNkyjaHcfuzvuXhyjqxbEDhp2P557QPo74DAAD__xj1kAM) to dismiss the separate state murder case, where trial is set to begin Sept. 8. Sentencing in the federal case is Dec. 18.
## Trump Asks Supreme Court to Allow Ballroom
President Trump [asked the Supreme Court](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOrCAUxvGnwU4DCOgUFLexm9tuaRAPyuYABo9j5u03s6-w9Zf8vuT_9ZyfLmLM23-XwFIoc4b7RCCCOieXt1gybFdEeh8ILgc8Kpyz5NK0fGyFnp2n-IJZuWa1AUBC34AVw2iGx0Nx1ezWh0U9QAm3KjWAklob0w_BaMcXs46mifbj8VFo0QvO-044D1Lo0fMgdM8FUxzWSKV23yVm2iHgu7ygdr6kBu1OdJys_8fkxOR033fn8-I_I5PTh2Zy4iOTk1BMTlSvdLSLQ6ylpPa8jgoJWl-uSu29R4J2L9cJ3U4Jm2rX446I8TQDU3xLLuLvLf2x1svKnwAAAP__X2p-xg) Friday to allow construction of the $400 million White House ballroom continue while the case is appealed, after a federal appeals court upheld an order blocking the project. This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College

Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0Utr3DAQAOBfI99s9PDz4EOCslBIWvqAHIVWGtsDsiQ88ob--7JhCz33OjPMN4_3N_NmMWBcv9odZiQyPnnjKMAHEuUjLemMHiPhuhUyksu-5mMtOmNdwRuY1lZ-7qQYl7GCWQxjP0xT23bVNveTWJQE4a_uerXWj0snejX1ICaQU9dWON_78VF0QgneqmZp5SC4HDs_St47y1p-Zm8LNPcJPJBLKecUsKCjJh1rFeatlExMPTF5YfKCcUnNhiGQtwEa8CeTl-UAqB3Vn0vVbjuQCtqI5Xftb56pCzmmNOdSqifOuXgVk_6m9ctPJvuz7IbSeThgSucjUQZXMK6P1A4ez50pDbvF8Ag6u2eLa2RKOzKfqvlXNXf1UZpigViY0s9fnl9fzPehfv_1o_57l-qYff7AEJD6gbV8vSuNS3tV_vNZt1n-CQAA__8hqqZN)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0Utr3DAQAOBfI99s9PDz4EOCslBIWvqAHIVWGtsDsiQ88ob--7JhCz33OjPMN4_3N_NmMWBcv9odZiQyPnnjKMAHEuUjLemMHiPhuhUyksu-5mMtOmNdwRuY1lZ-7qQYl7GCWQxjP0xT23bVNveTWJQE4a_uerXWj0snejX1ICaQU9dWON_78VF0QgneqmZp5SC4HDs_St47y1p-Zm8LNPcJPJBLKecUsKCjJh1rFeatlExMPTF5YfKCcUnNhiGQtwEa8CeTl-UAqB3Vn0vVbjuQCtqI5Xftb56pCzmmNOdSqifOuXgVk_6m9ctPJvuz7IbSeThgSucjUQZXMK6P1A4ez50pDbvF8Ag6u2eLa2RKOzKfqvlXNXf1UZpigViY0s9fnl9fzPehfv_1o_57l-qYff7AEJD6gbV8vSuNS3tV_vNZt1n-CQAA__8hqqZN)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** You probably know that C.S. Lewis also wrote the children's series, _The Chronicles of Narnia_. My wife and I read those books to our children so many times! I can't tell you how many dog-eared copies we have of these.

One of the best parts of this course is learning how the Christian faith is woven into these captivating stories. **I hope you 'll take advantage of this great FREE DVD offer today:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0Utr3DAQAOBfI99s9PDz4EOCslBIWvqAHIVWGtsDsiQ88ob--7JhCz33OjPMN4_3N_NmMWBcv9odZiQyPnnjKMAHEuUjLemMHiPhuhUyksu-5mMtOmNdwRuY1lZ-7qQYl7GCWQxjP0xT23bVNveTWJQE4a_uerXWj0snejX1ICaQU9dWON_78VF0QgneqmZp5SC4HDs_St47y1p-Zm8LNPcJPJBLKecUsKCjJh1rFeatlExMPTF5YfKCcUnNhiGQtwEa8CeTl-UAqB3Vn0vVbjuQCtqI5Xftb56pCzmmNOdSqifOuXgVk_6m9ctPJvuz7IbSeThgSucjUQZXMK6P1A4ez50pDbvF8Ag6u2eLa2RKOzKfqvlXNXf1UZpigViY0s9fnl9fzPehfv_1o_57l-qYff7AEJD6gbV8vSuNS3tV_vNZt1n-CQAA__8hqqZN)

Peter,
After two years of destruction of America under Trump, the people finally have their chance for payback. But he hasn't done it alone--no one has had his back more so than MAGA Speaker of the House Mike Johnson.
Mike Johnson is the head of the snake.
It was Johnson who ushered Trump's "big beautiful bill" through the House, the bill that ripped health care away from 12 million people and gutted SNAP, Medicaid, and student debt relief.

**I have some good news...and some bad news, Peter.**
**Let's get the bad news out of the way first:** Greg Abbott is already unleashing his $67 million war chest to drown out our message. His campaign is going up with a major ad buy in 9 media markets across Texas.
He's terrified. And he's going to spend whatever it takes to stop us.
**Now the good news:** We've had three separate polls in the last two weeks showing this race within 1 single point.
Since those polls dropped, the momentum has been incredible. This month alone, 33,000 grassroots supporters like you have contributed whatever amount they could give to our campaign.
And I’m extremely grateful for your support – it just goes to show how powerful this campaign really is and how badly people want to ditch Abbott. But we need to keep up. Abbott is about to flood the airwaves, and we can't afford to get drowned out.
So we're setting a huge goal of receiving **50,000 online donations from emails like these by August 16.**

| Dear Friend,
---
I’ve spent a lot of time ever since I awoke from my coma reflecting on the big picture of what my trial in Arizona is really all about.
---
I thought back to all the despicable things the vengeful Democrats have done to me...
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
__
---
_A dawn raid on my home.
Arresting me alongside President Trump as innocent men.
Freezing my bank accounts.
Seizing my assets.
Forcing me to the point of bankruptcy._
---
**And now, a vengeful Democrat Attorney General making me stand in a rigged trial for bogus state-level crimes, because she knows that not even the most powerful man on the face of the planet – President Trump – can save me with a _federal_ pardon in _state_ court.**
---
The lunatic Left’s desire to DESTROY yours truly knows no bounds.
---
They even stripped me of my law licenses so I would have no means to defend myself, leading pundits in the media to label me a **“ _DEAD_ _MAN_ _WALKING_!”**
---
But what I’ve come to realize ever since I came so close to death was that the pursuit of truth, freedom, and justice are worth infinitely more than any earthly possession.
---
**They can strip me of all I’m worth – _all I’ll ever be worth_ – but what I _REFUSE_ to surrender to the Democrats and their Deep State thugs is my LEGACY!**
---
And __that__ is what my final trial is truly all about, Friend.
---
**I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.”**
---
"__For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?_ " (Mark 8:36)_
---
You see, this FINAL BATTLE for my freedom is about ensuring this injustice can _NEVER_ _AGAIN_ happen to another innocent patriot all for standing by what he knows to be right and true.
---
I pray to God that will be my legacy when we win this trial.
---
But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: _good and honest Americans like _YOU__.
---
Friend, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it.
---
_**But if you can help, I’m going to need the best defense I can get to defeat this radical Democrat Attorney General who is hell-bent on locking me up for the rest of my life.**_
---
[**Please make a contribution to the Rudy Defense Trust to ensure I have the resources needed to retain a top-notch defense team in what is now the FINAL BATTLE for my freedom and justice.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---

Thank you and God bless you,

Rudy Giuliani

#

**_Please read:_
A personal appeal from Gabby Giffords **
Dear friends: I am reaching out to you today to **[respectfully ask if you can make a $3 contribution to GIFFORDS PAC.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/66845?c0=giff-em-q32026.bXvd9H&refcode=em260815-1-b&t=1&akid=11728%2E3935704%2E4JQNVw)
We knew that when Donald Trump was elected, there would be challenges ahead. Now, we are seeing firsthand that his administration and the MAGA-right are wasting no time trying to reverse our hard-fought progress on gun safety.
Some of the most extreme members of Congress have introduced bills to abolish the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), as well as advocating for national concealed carry reciprocity. Trump’s allies are also working to undo core parts of the gun safety progress made under President Biden and Vice President Harris’ tenure.
The challenges we’re up against aren’t easy, but I know a thing or two about getting through tough times.
I was shot in 2011, and I have been on a recovery journey every day since. Some days are harder than others, but even on the most difficult days, I refuse to give up hope. It’s the same way I refuse to give up hope for our gun violence prevention movement.
I will be fighting each and every day for a future free from gun violence, just as I have since GIFFORDS’s founding thirteen years ago. _I need you to stand with me in this fight._
**[Will you use this link to make a $3 contribution to GIFFORDS PAC before tonight’s August mid-month deadline?](https://go.giffords.org/go/66845?c0=giff-em-q32026.bXvd9H&refcode=em260815-1-b&t=2&akid=11728%2E3935704%2E4JQNVw)**

Dear Peter,

CNBC just named the "best place to live in America" - and for the fifth year in a row, _it 's Vermont_.

Their reasoning? **Vermont was the first state in the nation to enshrine abortion in its constitution, and CNBC gave it a perfect score, listing zero weaknesses.**

Minnesota came in at number four, and **CNBC praised Gov. Tim Walz (D)** for enshrining abortion into state law with his so-called "Protect Reproductive Options Act."

What they left out: Walz's long record of letting babies born alive after botched abortions be left to die.

You can't make this stuff up! And it just goes to show why our work at Students for Life Action is needed now more than ever before.

Senator Mark Warner is running this campaign the way he’s always run for office – getting out there, talking to Virginians, and humbly asking them to rehire him.

_But that’s not all._

_**By Eric J. Lullove, DPM -- for Blue Amp Media**_
Every dollar recovered from a Medicaid contractor that overbilled the public is, by law and by purpose, a dollar owed back to the people the program serves. In Florida, that means low-income children, medically fragile adults, and the safety-net providers who care for them. So when $10 million of a Medicaid fraud recovery is traced not into patient care but into a political committee that spent it defeating ballot initiatives, the question is not a partisan one. It is a health-care integrity question: who is entitled to money clawed back from a Medicaid contractor, and what happens when officials treat it as discretionary cash?
That is the core of what has become known as the Hope Florida scandal -- and it now sits at the center of Florida's 2026 U.S. Senate race.
## **The money and where it came from**
The chain begins with Centene, the nation's largest Medicaid managed-care company. Centene was accused of overbilling Florida's Medicaid program -- specifically, of its former pharmacy benefit manager keeping money owed to the state. The company settled with Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) for roughly $67 million. Of that, about $57 million was characterized as repayment of the Medicaid dollars themselves, with an additional sum offered to cover other alleged damages.**12**
This is ordinary, if unglamorous, health-care enforcement. Managed-care overbilling is one of the most persistent problems in the Medicaid program, and recoveries like this exist precisely to make the program -- and its beneficiaries -- whole.
What happened next was not ordinary. Instead of the full recovery flowing back through AHCA to serve its statutory purpose, $10 million was directed to the Hope Florida Foundation, the direct-support nonprofit tied to First Lady Casey DeSantis's signature Hope Florida initiative. A direct-support organization of that kind is bound by Florida law to specific transparency obligations -- a published mission, a multi-year plan, a code of ethics, public tax records, and annual audits. During legislative questioning, lawmakers noted the foundation appeared not to have met several of those requirements.**3**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.7UgIQm9evuWBvIgdMqxUkT6TMxwIb1uU5bco-yJdqKQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=211242737)
## **From a children 's charity to a political committee**
The $10 million did not stay at Hope Florida long. According to a Florida House inquiry led by Republican Rep. Alex Andrade of Pensacola, the foundation transferred the money to two nonprofits -- Secure Florida's Future and Save Our Society from Drugs. Those groups, in turn, routed roughly $8.5 million to Keep Florida Clean, a political committee then chaired by James Uthmeier, at the time Gov. Ron DeSantis's chief of staff.**45**
Keep Florida Clean spent heavily against two measures on Florida's November 2024 ballot: Amendment 3, which would have legalized recreational marijuana, and Amendment 4, which would have restored abortion rights in the state constitution. Amendment 3 drew 56 percent support but fell short of Florida's 60 percent threshold.**5**
Andrade's assessment was blunt. He described the transfers as Medicaid funds steered through intermediary organizations into a political committee, and told a House Health Care Budget Subcommittee hearing that he believed the transaction was illegal.**4**
The DeSantis administration disputes the framing. AHCA's general counsel wrote to legislative leaders arguing that the $10 million came from the portion of the Centene settlement covering "other alleged damages" rather than recouped Medicaid dollars, and that the law does not prohibit negotiating settlement conditions requiring a released party to take actions beyond paying money to the state. In other words: the administration's position is that this was not, strictly, Medicaid money being diverted.**6**
That distinction -- whether the $10 million was recovered Medicaid funding or a separate damages payment -- is the pivot on which much of the legal argument turns. It has not been resolved in public. And it is precisely the kind of question a complete evidentiary record would settle.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/67a51537-7110-4a66-8dad-503647b67b73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **Where Ashley Moody fits**
Ashley Moody was Florida's attorney general when the Centene settlement was finalized. She was later appointed by Gov. DeSantis to the U.S. Senate seat vacated when Marco Rubio became Secretary of State, and she is now running in 2026 to hold it. Uthmeier succeeded her as attorney general.**7**
Reporting by CBS News Miami stated that Moody's office signed off on the settlement without imposing the safeguards or oversight her office would ordinarily require to ensure recovered funds were properly spent -- the same kind of guidance, critics note, that the attorney general's office routinely provides to other parties. Moody has not, according to that reporting, answered direct questions from journalists or from Andrade about what she knew regarding the eventual political use of the funds or whether her office coordinated with the governor's office. Her declining to engage those questions is not, by itself, evidence of wrongdoing -- but it leaves the public without an account from the one office positioned to give one.**8**
Her campaign, for its part, has characterized the settlement as an AHCA agreement negotiated and settled through AHCA and outside counsel, and has said the underlying information is already public. _It is a defense of process, not a rebuttal of the money trail._
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.7UgIQm9evuWBvIgdMqxUkT6TMxwIb1uU5bco-yJdqKQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=211242737)
## **The report no one has seen**
A Leon County grand jury was convened to investigate the Hope Florida transactions. As of this writing, no indictments have been issued, and no grand jury report has been publicly released. Whether a final report has even been completed remains unconfirmed.**9**
Here the accountability question sharpens. The Florida Center for Government Accountability has said publicly _**that Moody is likely objecting to the release of the grand jury investigation**_. Democratic Senate candidate Alex Vindman has gone further, saying he suspects Moody is the reason the report has not been made public and challenging her to call for its release: if she has nothing to hide, he argues, she should demand the record come out.**1011**
_**Moody 's campaign says the opposite -- that she has had no role in any grand jury proceedings and would welcome the report's release**_. Those two accounts sit in tension, and only one point is independently verifiable: _**to date, Moody has not publicly called for the report to be released.**_ She may have sound legal reasons for that, or none at all; the record does not yet say. But for a former state attorney general now seeking a full Senate term, whose office finalized the settlement at the origin of this money, whether she asks for the record to come out is a fair question for voters to weigh.**11**
The remedy is not rhetorical. A grand jury report -- or a clear statement from the state attorney on its status -- would establish, on the record, whether recovered Medicaid-adjacent funds were lawfully redirected or improperly converted to political use. Every official with the standing to seek that record and declining to do so is making a choice about how much the public gets to know.
## **Why this is a health-care story, not just a political one**
It is easy to file Hope Florida under campaign-season intrigue. That would be a mistake. The mechanism at issue -- a Medicaid contractor's overbilling recovery, redirected away from the program that was defrauded -- strikes at the trust that makes Medicaid enforcement possible in the first place. Recoveries exist so that beneficiaries and the taxpayers who fund their care are made whole. When those dollars are treated as a flexible pool for other purposes, the loss is not abstract: it is care not delivered, oversight not exercised, and a precedent set that settlement money can be steered wherever the politically powerful prefer.
Florida recovered money because a company took more than it was owed from a program built for the vulnerable. The public is owed a straightforward accounting of where that money went, and why. Until the record is opened, the most consequential question remains unanswered -- and the responsibility for opening it rests with the officials who have the standing to ask.

How a Medicaid overbilling settlement ended up funding a political campaign -- and why a sitting U.S. Senator has still not called for the record to be opened | | and | Aug 15 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- By Eric J. Lullove, DPM -- for Blue Amp Media Every dollar recovered from a Medicaid contractor that overbilled the public is, by law and by purpose, a dollar owed back to the people the program serves. In Florida, that means low-income children, medically fragile adults, and the safety-net providers who care for them. So when $10 million of a Medicaid fraud recovery is traced not into patient care but into a political committee that spent it defeating ballot initiatives, the question is not a partisan one. It is a health-care integrity question: who is entitled to money clawed back from a Medicaid contractor, and what happens when officials treat it as discretionary cash? That is the core of what has become known as the Hope Florida scandal -- and it now sits at the center of Florida's 2026 U.S. Senate race. The money and where it came from The chain begins with Centene, the nation's largest Medicaid managed-care company. Centene was accused of overbilling Florida's Medicaid program -- specifically, of its former pharmacy benefit manager keeping money owed to the state. The company settled with Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) for roughly $67 million. Of that, about $57 million was characterized as repayment of the Medicaid dollars themselves, with an additional sum offered to cover other alleged damages.12 This is ordinary, if unglamorous, health-care enforcement. Managed-care overbilling is one of the most persistent problems in the Medicaid program, and recoveries like this exist precisely to make the program -- and its beneficiaries -- whole. What happened next was not ordinary. Instead of the full recovery flowing back through AHCA to serve its statutory purpose, $10 million was directed to the Hope Florida Foundation, the direct-support nonprofit tied to First Lady Casey DeSantis's signature Hope Florida initiative. A direct-support organization of that kind is bound by Florida law to specific transparency obligations -- a published mission, a multi-year plan, a code of ethics, public tax records, and annual audits. During legislative questioning, lawmakers noted the foundation appeared not to have met several of those requirements.3 From a children 's charity to a political committee The $10 million did not stay at Hope Florida long. According to a Florida House inquiry led by Republican Rep. Alex Andrade of Pensacola, the foundation transferred the money to two nonprofits -- Secure Florida's Future and Save Our Society from Drugs. Those groups, in turn, routed roughly $8.5 million to Keep Florida Clean, a political committee then chaired by James Uthmeier, at the time Gov. Ron DeSantis's chief of staff.45 Keep Florida Clean spent heavily against two measures on Florida's November 2024 ballot: Amendment 3, which would have legalized recreational marijuana, and Amendment 4, which would have restored abortion rights in the state constitution. Amendment 3 drew 56 percent support but fell short of Florida's 60 percent threshold.5 Andrade's assessment was blunt. He described the transfers as Medicaid funds steered through intermediary organizations into a political committee, and told a House Health Care Budget Subcommittee hearing that he believed the transaction was illegal.4 The DeSantis administration disputes the framing. AHCA's general counsel wrote to legislative leaders arguing that the $10 million came from the portion of the Centene settlement covering "other alleged damages" rather than recouped Medicaid dollars, and that the law does not prohibit negotiating settlement conditions requiring a released party to take actions beyond paying money to the state. In other words: the administration's position is that this was not, strictly, Medicaid money being diverted.6 That distinction -- whether the $10 million was recovered Medicaid funding or a separate damages payment -- is the pivot on which much of the legal argument turns. It has not been resolved in public. And it is precisely the kind of question a complete evidentiary record would settle. | | ---|---|--- Where Ashley Moody fits Ashley Moody was Florida's attorney general when the Centene settlement was finalized. She was later appointed by Gov. DeSantis to the U.S. Senate seat vacated when Marco Rubio became Secretary of State, and she is now running in 2026 to hold it. Uthmeier succeeded her as attorney general.7 Reporting by CBS News Miami stated that Moody's office signed off on the settlement without imposing the safeguards or oversight her office would ordinarily require to ensure recovered funds were properly spent -- the same kind of guidance, critics note, that the attorney general's office routinely provides to other parties. Moody has not, according to that reporting, answered direct questions from journalists or from Andrade about what she knew regarding the eventual political use of the funds or whether her office coordinated with the governor's office. Her declining to engage those questions is not, by itself, evidence of wrongdoing -- but it leaves the public without an account from the one office positioned to give one.8 Her campaign, for its part, has characterized the settlement as an AHCA agreement negotiated and settled through AHCA and outside counsel, and has said the underlying information is already public. It is a defense of process, not a rebuttal of the money trail. The report no one has seen A Leon County grand jury was convened to investigate the Hope Florida transactions. As of this writing, no indictments have been issued, and no grand jury report has been publicly released. Whether a final report has even been completed remains unconfirmed.9 Here the accountability question sharpens. The Florida Center for Government Accountability has said publicly that Moody is likely objecting to the release of the grand jury investigation. Democratic Senate candidate Alex Vindman has gone further, saying he suspects Moody is the reason the report has not been made public and challenging her to call for its release: if she has nothing to hide, he argues, she should demand the record come out.1011 Moody 's campaign says the opposite -- that she has had no role in any grand jury proceedings and would welcome the report's release. Those two accounts sit in tension, and only one point is independently verifiable: to date, Moody has not publicly called for the report to be released. She may have sound legal reasons for that, or none at all; the record does not yet say. But for a former state attorney general now seeking a full Senate term, whose office finalized the settlement at the origin of this money, whether she asks for the record to come out is a fair question for voters to weigh.11 The remedy is not rhetorical. A grand jury report -- or a clear statement from the state attorney on its status -- would establish, on the record, whether recovered Medicaid-adjacent funds were lawfully redirected or improperly converted to political use. Every official with the standing to seek that record and declining to do so is making a choice about how much the public gets to know. Why this is a health-care story, not just a political one It is easy to file Hope Florida under campaign-season intrigue. That would be a mistake. The mechanism at issue -- a Medicaid contractor's overbilling recovery, redirected away from the program that was defrauded -- strikes at the trust that makes Medicaid enforcement possible in the first place. Recoveries exist so that beneficiaries and the taxpayers who fund their care are made whole. When those dollars are treated as a flexible pool for other purposes, the loss is not abstract: it is care not delivered, oversight not exercised, and a precedent set that settlement money can be steered wherever the politically powerful prefer. Florida recovered money because a company took more than it was owed from a program built for the vulnerable. The public is owed a straightforward accounting of where that money went, and why. Until the record is opened, the most consequential question remains unanswered -- and the responsibility for opening it rests with the officials who have the standing to ask. Cliff 's Note: This one's free. On purpose. Ten million dollars clawed back from a Medicaid contractor never made it to the kids it was owed to. It went through a foundation, through two nonprofits, and $8.5 million of it landed in a political committee fighting Amendment 4. A Republican legislator traced it and called it illegal. A grand jury looked at it. The report is still sealed. Ashley Moody's office signed the settlement. She says she'd welcome the report's release. She's never asked for it. Dr. Eric Lullove laid the whole thing out. No paywall, because every voter in Florida should be able to read it before they vote. Live with Alex Vindman at 4:30 Eastern today. Peter,

they do it by making someone else pay the price. They go after immigrants.

corporations get heard first, and working families get told to wait.

Our movement believes in something simpler: a country where people have
what they need, where no one's neighbor gets left behind, and where
everyone — not just the well-connected — gets to live with dignity and
actually afford their life.

And people are already building it themselves, in their own neighborhoods
and communities, without waiting for permission.

at all. No corporate PAC bankrolled us. No party machine cleared our path.

People decided they were done waiting, and they backed leaders who'd say
so out loud and fight unapologetically for the working class.

Primary season is almost over. We've got less than 90 days until Election
Day, and every dollar we bring in before tonight's deadline goes straight
toward defending our seats and keeping this fight going.

But actions speak louder than social media, and her actions tell us that **Miller-Meeks is a dangerous threat to the future of Social Security _and_ Medicare.**

She has supported privatizing both Social Security and Medicare, which would put at risk the guaranteed benefits seniors have paid into. She blamed the high cost of health care on Medicare. She has even called for raising the retirement age for Social Security. Worse, she voted _against_ allowing Medicare to negotiate for lower drug prices, _against_ capping seniors' out-of-pocket drug expenses, and _against_ capping the cost of insulin at $35 per month for seniors on Medicare.

Are you outraged? [**Christina is, and she needs your help to go to Congress and actually protect and strengthen the programs our communities depend on. Will you make a donation to help us reach our campaign's $10,000 mid-month goal?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137286040/640276384/-2016015222?refcode=em26_260815_MM2_fnd_gq_act___DDCB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260815_MM2_fnd_gq_act___DDCB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=ceae03fd-b998-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZWFlMDNmZC1iOTk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VJVNzqAbBXstyo03iPsAKgv-qgRedEAmeSsU9QNo3zg=)

Now here's what real commitment looks like. In Congress, Christina will:
* Protect Medicare and Social Security, and shore up the Social Security trust funds to fully fund them for future generations.
* Stop those in Washington who seek to cut, privatize, or jeopardize these critical programs.
* Allow Iowans to buy into Medicare at any age, which would protect Iowans in their fifties and early sixties from paying outrageous health insurance premiums.
* Allow Medicare to negotiate for lower prices on more drugs so seniors and other taxpayers pay less.

Two more years of that? My goal is to leave everything on the field and send Christina straight to Congress to be the champion for Social Security and Medicare we know she will be. = \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Team Bohannan Date: August 14, 2026 Subject: Actions speak louder than social media posts = Peter, last month Mariannette Miller-Meeks posted that she was "committed to protecting and strengthening Social Security." But actions speak louder than social media, and her actions tell us that Miller-Meeks is a dangerous threat to the future of Social Security and Medicare. She has supported privatizing both Social Security and Medicare, which would put at risk the guaranteed benefits seniors have paid into. She blamed the high cost of health care on Medicare. She has even called for raising the retirement age for Social Security. Worse, she voted against allowing Medicare to negotiate for lower drug prices, against capping seniors' out-of-pocket drug expenses, and against capping the cost of insulin at $35 per month for seniors on Medicare. Are you outraged? = Now here's what real commitment looks like. In Congress, Christina will: Protect Medicare and Social Security, and shore up the Social Security trust funds to fully fund them for future generations. Stop those in Washington who seek to cut, privatize, or jeopardize these critical programs. Allow Iowans to buy into Medicare at any age, which would protect Iowans in their fifties and early sixties from paying outrageous health insurance premiums. Allow Medicare to negotiate for lower prices on more drugs so seniors and other taxpayers pay less. Expand Medicare to cover dental, vision, and hearing care. Expand Medicare to cover home health costs incurred by family caregivers. It's about time someone spoke up for Iowans' Social Security and Medicare, and Christina has the will and the focus to be that fighter in Washington. = If you've saved your payment information with I was recently back in my hometown helping a friend clean out a house that he bought in my old neighborhood. Today, I'm going to do something a little different than usual, I'm simply going to report my interactions with the neighbors. No analysis, no opinions, just a brief glimpse of a place that I have full access to and many of you have never experienced.
Warning: You might not like parts of this. But it is exactly how things went down over the course of three days in a declining American neighborhood, no exaggerations or modifications.
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Xid6OTbDk0iX6FheAFWWSY3jTqY1AAQegKIwNnfDItk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=211305816)
I love going back to my old neighborhood. Because I don't spend a lot of time there anymore, whenever I walk the streets I get hit with all sorts of flashbacks.
The small ones are my favorites.
The curb where I picked rocks out of my leg after crashing my scooter. A driveway I shoveled where the guy tipped me five extra bucks. My wet hair freezing on the walk to the bus stop. You get the idea.
So when I had the excuse to go back to town recently to help clean out an old house a friend of mine had purchased, I took it.
I landed Sunday morning and got to the house that afternoon. My friend unexpectedly had to cover a shift at the restaurant he works at, so I ended up all by myself and completely unprepared the first day of work-- but determined to impress him by getting as much done as I could solo!
There were some masks, regular brooms, a dustpan, trash bags, and gloves at the house already. But there was some big furniture I would now want to try to haul out on my own and a lot of debris on the floor. So I needed to track down a dolly and a push broom, two things I wasn't about to just buy for a couple days work.
Fortunately, I thought I had a lead. Half a minute later, a slightly disheveled older man cracked the door open with his right hand, holding his truly vicious looking dog back with the left, and peeked out.
"Hey, how's it going?" I said.
Shirtless and wearing jeans, he looked me up and down while trying to hush up his dog so he could hear.
"Hold on a sec," he shouted, "Let me put him away."
He closed the door and I heard him and the dog fade away into the house.
I sat down on the concrete post at the top of the stairs and looked around while I waited. The porch was extremely neat and clean, like someone swept it every morning. A couple of black metal chairs sat on the right side of the door and a wooden one sat to its left. A decorative cross hung between two windows and a couple of small, concrete, religion-themed statuettes, like you find on many Missouri porches and yards, rounded out the exterior decor. I think there was an empty bird feeder and maybe an empty hanging plant pot, too, but I can't remember for sure. Everything was worn and showed its age, but was well taken care of.
The reason I remember everything so well is because I basically had an eternity to look around with nothing else to do. A minute or so after the man and his dog had left, the house had gone quiet and there wasn't any more sign of movement or noise inside for at least five minutes. I actually think it was more like ten, but ten minutes is a pretty long time and people usually overestimate time when they're waiting so I don't want to over estimate here. But it was long enough that I began to wonder if he was going to come back at all, and had started assessing the dolly-and-broom potential of other houses nearby when I finally heard another sound at the door.
The man was back!
As he walked through the doorway he proclaimed, in good spirits, that I'd better not be selling something, then sat down in the metal chair closest to the door and smiled, waiting for me to talk.
He was now wearing a clean wrinkle-free t-shirt, a black mariner hat, nice shoes, and I swear he had even taken the time to comb his white mustache. Out in the light he looked to be somewhere in his mid seventies and I guessed from his current meticulous presentation that he didn't get many, if any, visitors, and wanted to make a good impression.
"Even worse," I retorted, "I'm just here to mooch off ya!"
He chuckled and sat down.
"Alright, let's here it."
I explained that I was cleaning out the house next door and realized I didn't have a dolly or push broom. "I heard you out on the back porch earlier jamming some classic tunes and after a look at how you take care of your place, figured you might be the type of guy who would have those sorts of things."
Shameless flattery, I know. Busted. But who wants to move a whole rotten refrigerator out of a house by themselves without a dolly?
He feigned embarrassment, seemed pleased with himself, said something about how he liked blue-toothing his music back there, and then asked me if I was his new neighbor.
"No, Sir, I'm just doing some work for the guy who owns it. I'm Lucas by the way." We shook hands and introduced ourselves.
"Well that's too bad," he said. "And sorry about earlier," referring to his dog, "He gets a little excited whenever someone comes around. It's just me and him now, my wife passed away a few years ago, so there's not too much going on."
"No worries. I hope you're holding up ok without her. He seems like a good dog to have around if you're by yourself. I know the neighborhood can be a little rough sometimes."
"You know, it's mostly pretty quiet."
"I believe that," I replied, "It used to be wild around here, I grew up in this neighborhood and there were kids running everywhere back then."
"Hmmm, well, that would sure beat what we have across the street these days."
"Oh, what's that?"
"Oh, you know. Just a thousand people crammed in that house. Random folks coming and going all the time. Parking on the wrong side of the street. Facing every which way. Going to cause an accident sooner or later. Not to mention partying and yelling and all that."
As he spoke, he became more and more animated, and it was clear this was something he dwelled on.
"Damn, that sucks," I said, following the line of his finger toward a house across the street and up from him.
"You be it does. I've gotten into it with some of em over and over again about coming on my property. You know what the worst thing is, though? You can't even call the cops. They don't do nothin. You know what happened the last time I called?"
"What?"
"They sent out some _woman_ cop who couldn't do a damn thing. Shameful. Just shameful. I sat right here on my porch and watched the whole thing. The man who lives there just blew his dope in her face and told her to fuck off and you know what happened next? She just did! Can you believe that? She just did like he told her. Up and left. You know what woulda happened if I'd done that? I'd be thrown in jail. That's what. Straight away. But him? Nothing. That's the world we're living in now. And she just drove off."
"Wow," I said, giving him some space to cool off.
He pulled out a cigarette, loaded it into a white plastic holder, lit it and smoked for a minute, glaring at the house across the street. Then he looked at me.
"You know what? I do have a dolly and broom I can lend you. Can you do me a favor, though?"
"Maybe, what's up?"
"I need you to tell the owner something for me."
"Yeah?"
"First, though, do you know is he going to rent it or live in it?"
"I think he's going rent it," I replied.
"That's what I figured. Now I'm not against a guy making a buck. I don't have a problem with that. So it's not that..." He paused and seemed to be choosing his next words carefully. "And I know I'm not supposed to say it like this, but... I just don't care anymore."
He was getting animated again.
"I'm old enough that I'm gonna say what I mean. And I want you to let him know that if he moves any n*****s or Mexicans in there, well there's just gonna be trouble."
So that _had_ been a glimpse of confederate flag tattoo I'd caught when he first opened the door.
He gave a cautious sideways look, as if this statement had been a way to try to gauge where I stood on things. I wanted to make it clear that I wasn't with him on this, but not in a way that would end the conversation because my friend, the homeowner, is Mexican, and I wanted to try to find out what this could mean for him.
"Is that right?" I asked.
The neighbor took a long searching look at my face and thought about things for a second.
"Yes, Sir, it is," he implored, as if he was now trying to convince me rather than gauge me.
"I'm tired of 'em all. The one, like them over there," he waved in the direction of the house across the street, "don't work and just cause trouble. As for the Mexicans, I've seen who he's got working there on that house and I'd bet a silver dollar that he's thinking about letting some migrants live in there. It's not right. Them thinking they can just take over everything."
He took a drag on his cigarette. I waited.
"Do you know if that's his plan or not?" He asked.
"As I understand it," I figured it was best to just be straight with him, "He's going to rent it on the open market, like on Zillow or something, to whoever can pay the rent and deposit. If it doesn't rent, he may rent it to a friend or a worker. I don't know, it's his house. He's not gonna discriminate, though, I'm sure of that. So I imagine you're probably just gonna need to accept that whatever happens happens, and accept it. I'm positive he's not gonna have troublemakers in there, though."
"Hmph," he grumbled.
"And," I added, "It'll definitely be an upgrade over who was in there before."
"You mean "A"?" he replied, seeming excited at the chance to sort-of change the subject. "Nah, he was alright. His problem is he was just dumb as bricks, that's all."
I gave him a skeptical look. I knew the previous tenant, if you can call him that.
"Dumb? Is that what they're calling it now?" I laughed pointedly. "I went to school with that guy. He was squatting there and turned it into some sort of drug den and filled it up with a bunch of other squatters. I'm cleaning out his trash right now, it's disgusting."
"Well, maybe he was a little crazy, too," the neighbor said awkwardly, "But I never had any trouble with him!"
"Well, that's good," I said, "because I think he might actually still be your neighbor. I saw a bunch of mattresses, tarps, and boxes in the woods back there."
He glanced in the direction of the woods and shifted in his chair, clearly not thrilled at the idea of "A" still being around. He mulled things over again, dragging on his cigarette.
I returned to brainstorming a secondary source for a dolly and a push broom.
Suddenly, out of the blue, he asked me a question.
"Do you ever watch Newsmax?"
I laughed again, but this time only in my head. Apparently he was in the mood for second chances.
"No," I answered, "I don't really watch much of anything outside of some Netflix shows with my wife, but I'm sure that type of thing is up my ally."
"You've really got to." His eyes actually lit up. "I mean really. I'm telling you. There's this guy on there, Carl Higbie, he's a Navy Seal. He just doesn't give a fuck. Man says right there on national TV he'd shoot anyone who came on his lawn or caused him a problem. You really gotta watch it."
He paused, and added with a flourish: "It's admirable."
What a curious choice of a word, I thought.
Also curious, I thought, was the fact that by default I appeared to be in a club that I never gave any indication I shared a single value with. The only information this man knew about me was my first name, that I am white, somewhere around 40, grew up in the neighborhood, and was working on the house. I was wearing a sweat-soaked dusty and grimy gray t-shirt and a pair of work pants (the house didn't have power or AC) and I needed to borrow a dolly and push broom. And I hadn't engaged positively with any of his sentiments.
"I mean, I'm a marine, so I guess it's cool that he was in the military, but I think I'll just stick with Love is Blind," was my answer.
"Hmmm. Well, I think you'd like it if you gave it a try," he said, standing up, and not seeming to care that I am a Marine, which was interesting, and apparently oblivious to the existence of the American classic known as Love is Blind.
I stood up, too. He tamped out his cigarette and put the holder in his pocket.
"Come along now, let's get you what you need."
In a bit of shock that this was still happening, I followed him around the side of the house to the back. His dog, now on the back porch, went viciously crazy again the second we turned the corner. He half-heartedly told him to shut up, which had no effect, and unlocked and opened his garage.
"Just give me a sec," he said, "I was welding up the trailer the other day so I gotta get this off of here."
I looked around the garage as he unstrapped some welding equipment from the dolly he was apparently about to lend me. I had been in this garage a couple of times as a kid and was flashing back to what it used to look like. Presently, it held several sparkling Harleys and a bunch of work stuff.
He rolled the empty dolly over to me and asked, "Now where'd that broom go?"
The question was clearly directed to himself, but when he headed the opposite direction of the one I'd seen in the corner, I answered it anyway.
"I think I saw one over there," I said, pointing in the corner, "Although I don't know if it's the one you're looking for."
He looked over and sure enough it was.
We stepped outside and he yelled over the barking "Just put 'em back here when you're done with 'em." And he went back inside.
Later that afternoon, as I worked cleaning out the house, sure enough, random cars would occasionally roll up out front on the street and another older man, this one maybe in his 60s, would come out to meet them, talk for a minute and go back inside.
At one point, while I was struggling to take apart an old piece of furniture so that it would fit through the door, two cars sped up out front a minute or two apart from one other. The second vehicle parked the wrong direction on the street and quite crookedly, exactly as the neighbor had complained about earlier. Two young men exited the crooked car and two young women the other. This time, the older man didn't come out to meet them.
The crooked car left its loud music on and they started having an animated, but friendly, conversation out front while it blared.
I really needed a screwdriver for this furniture, but I didn't want to go next door again, so I thought what the hell, might as well meet all the neighbors, and went out front. I walked up to the young group and shouted "Do any of you all live here?" and pointed across the street.
The guys looked at me but didn't answer. One of the women smiled and waved and yelled that she did. I asked her if by any chance she had a Philips screwdriver I could borrow. She said the pointy one? I said yeah. She said of course, if she had one I could, and waved for me to follow her up the walk.
I found myself waiting on yet another neighborhood porch while the guys hung out by their car. I wondered if the the neighbor from earlier could see me out there and if so, if he would now be wanting his broom and dolly back.
The woman brought out two options for me, one almost completely rusted through and the other one broken on the end, but serviceable. I said thanks and asked if I should just bring it back or leave it on the porch or something. Jovially, she said anything works, but they were usually around so it wouldn't be a problem either way.
When I got the furniture apart, the two young men were still in their wrongly parked car, but the women seemed to have gone inside, so I walked across and knocked on the door. A four-year-old-ish little girl answered. I asked her if she could find a grown up so I could give them back some tools, and the older gentleman who I had seen greeting cars earlier came and took them from me without saying a word. Pushing my luck, I asked if I could borrow some scissors for two minutes to cut a wire. He grunted and brought me some, which I returned a few minutes later. I thanked him and he nodded in response.
The next day I saw him sitting on his porch when I was preparing to take some photos and video of the work I had done out front. I walked over and let him know that he might end up in some of them if he was out front, in case that mattered to him. This time he laughed and said no problem, he wasn't worried about it, and wished me good luck on the work.
I saw the young woman again later at the smoke shop/mini-mart on the corner when I was buying a $7 bottle of orange juice and a $4 off-brand mini Hostess pie. This was the only location for food anywhere nearby. She and the cashier were bantering back and forth about the merits of Miami Mint flavored vape and paid me no attention.
As I sat on the front step of the house in the 100 degree heat eating my pie, I reminisced about how once a month, on payday, my dad used take us to the now-bulldozed neighborhood grocery store to pick out one of these pies, and how when I was little I always sucked out the inside before eating the crust.
The dolly-and-push-broom neighbor drove by in his immaculately washed mid-90's pickup. He waved hello and I waved back. Either he hadn't seen me cavorting with his enemy or had decided he didn't care.
That was the only other time I saw him. I kept his stuff for three days before putting it back behind his garage, and he never complained or came to find it.
On my way out of town, I relayed my earlier conversation with him to my Mexican friend who owns the house.
He was astonished, said the guy had always been nice to him and they had complained together about the folks across the street and even about the squatter who used to live there (and who continued to occasionally break in and did in fact still live off and on in the nearby woods).
I guess that's America.
Lucas

The one, like them over there," he waved in the direction of the house across the street, "don't work and just cause trouble. As for the Mexicans, I've seen who he's got working there on that house and I'd bet a silver dollar that he's thinking about letting some migrants live in there. It's not right. Them thinking they can just take over everything." He took a drag on his cigarette. I waited. "Do you know if that's his plan or not?" He asked. "As I understand it," I figured it was best to just be straight with him, "He's going to rent it on the open market, like on Zillow or something, to whoever can pay the rent and deposit. If it doesn't rent, he may rent it to a friend or a worker. I don't know, it's his house. He's not gonna discriminate, though, I'm sure of that. So I imagine you're probably just gonna need to accept that whatever happens happens, and accept it. I'm positive he's not gonna have troublemakers in there, though." "Hmph," he grumbled. "And," I added, "It'll definitely be an upgrade over who was in there before." "You mean "A"?" he replied, seeming excited at the chance to sort-of change the subject. "Nah, he was alright. His problem is he was just dumb as bricks, that's all." I gave him a skeptical look. I knew the previous tenant, if you can call him that. "Dumb? Is that what they're calling it now?" I laughed pointedly. "I went to school with that guy. He was squatting there and turned it into some sort of drug den and filled it up with a bunch of other squatters. I'm cleaning out his trash right now, it's disgusting." "Well, maybe he was a little crazy, too," the neighbor said awkwardly, "But I never had any trouble with him!" "Well, that's good," I said, "because I think he might actually still be your neighbor. I saw a bunch of mattresses, tarps, and boxes in the woods back there." He glanced in the direction of the woods and shifted in his chair, clearly not thrilled at the idea of "A" still being around. He mulled things over again, dragging on his cigarette. I returned to brainstorming a secondary source for a dolly and a push broom. Suddenly, out of the blue, he asked me a question. "Do you ever watch Newsmax?" I laughed again, but this time only in my head. Apparently he was in the mood for second chances. "No," I answered, "I don't really watch much of anything outside of some Netflix shows with my wife, but I'm sure that type of thing is up my ally." "You've really got to." His eyes actually lit up. "I mean really. I'm telling you. There's this guy on there, Carl Higbie, he's a Navy Seal. He just doesn't give a fuck. Man says right there on national TV he'd shoot anyone who came on his lawn or caused him a problem. You really gotta watch it." He paused, and added with a flourish: "It's admirable." What a curious choice of a word, I thought. Also curious, I thought, was the fact that by default I appeared to be in a club that I never gave any indication I shared a single value with. The only information this man knew about me was my first name, that I am white, somewhere around 40, grew up in the neighborhood, and was working on the house. I was wearing a sweat-soaked dusty and grimy gray t-shirt and a pair of work pants (the house didn't have power or AC) and I needed to borrow a dolly and push broom. And I hadn't engaged positively with any of his sentiments. "I mean, I'm a marine, so I guess it's cool that he was in the military, but I think I'll just stick with Love is Blind," was my answer. "Hmmm. Well, I think you'd like it if you gave it a try," he said, standing up, and not seeming to care that I am a Marine, which was interesting, and apparently oblivious to the existence of the American classic known as Love is Blind. I stood up, too. He tamped out his cigarette and put the holder in his pocket. "Come along now, let's get you what you need." In a bit of shock that this was still happening, I followed him around the side of the house to the back. His dog, now on the back porch, went viciously crazy again the second we turned the corner. He half-heartedly told him to shut up, which had no effect, and unlocked and opened his garage. "Just give me a sec," he said, "I was welding up the trailer the other day so I gotta get this off of here." I looked around the garage as he unstrapped some welding equipment from the dolly he was apparently about to lend me. I had been in this garage a couple of times as a kid and was flashing back to what it used to look like. Presently, it held several sparkling Harleys and a bunch of work stuff. He rolled the empty dolly over to me and asked, "Now where'd that broom go?" The question was clearly directed to himself, but when he headed the opposite direction of the one I'd seen in the corner, I answered it anyway. "I think I saw one over there," I said, pointing in the corner, "Although I don't know if it's the one you're looking for." He looked over and sure enough it was. We stepped outside and he yelled over the barking "Just put 'em back here when you're done with 'em." And he went back inside. Later that afternoon, as I worked cleaning out the house, sure enough, random cars would occasionally roll up out front on the street and another older man, this one maybe in his 60s, would come out to meet them, talk for a minute and go back inside. At one point, while I was struggling to take apart an old piece of furniture so that it would fit through the door, two cars sped up out front a minute or two apart from one other. The second vehicle parked the wrong direction on the street and quite crookedly, exactly as the neighbor had complained about earlier. Two young men exited the crooked car and two young women the other. This time, the older man didn't come out to meet them. The crooked car left its loud music on and they started having an animated, but friendly, conversation out front while it blared. I really needed a screwdriver for this furniture, but I didn't want to go next door again, so I thought what the hell, might as well meet all the neighbors, and went out front. I walked up to the young group and shouted "Do any of you all live here?" and pointed across the street. The guys looked at me but didn't answer. One of the women smiled and waved and yelled that she did. I asked her if by any chance she had a Philips screwdriver I could borrow. She said the pointy one? I said yeah. She said of course, if she had one I could, and waved for me to follow her up the walk. I found myself waiting on yet another neighborhood porch while the guys hung out by their car. I wondered if the the neighbor from earlier could see me out there and if so, if he would now be wanting his broom and dolly back. The woman brought out two options for me, one almost completely rusted through and the other one broken on the end, but serviceable. I said thanks and asked if I should just bring it back or leave it on the porch or something. Jovially, she said anything works, but they were usually around so it wouldn't be a problem either way. When I got the furniture apart, the two young men were still in their wrongly parked car, but the women seemed to have gone inside, so I walked across and knocked on the door. A four-year-old-ish little girl answered. I asked her if she could find a grown up so I could give them back some tools, and the older gentleman who I had seen greeting cars earlier came and took them from me without saying a word. Pushing my luck, I asked if I could borrow some scissors for two minutes to cut a wire. He grunted and brought me some, which I returned a few minutes later. I thanked him and he nodded in response. The next day I saw him sitting on his porch when I was preparing to take some photos and video of the work I had done out front. I walked over and let him know that he might end up in some of them if he was out front, in case that mattered to him. This time he laughed and said no problem, he wasn't worried about it, and wished me good luck on the work. I saw the young woman again later at the smoke shop/mini-mart on the corner when I was buying a $7 bottle of orange juice and a $4 off-brand mini Hostess pie. This was the only location for food anywhere nearby. She and the cashier were bantering back and forth about the merits of Miami Mint flavored vape and paid me no attention. As I sat on the front step of the house in the 100 degree heat eating my pie, I reminisced about how once a month, on payday, my dad used take us to the now-bulldozed neighborhood grocery store to pick out one of these pies, and how when I was little I always sucked out the inside before eating the crust. The dolly-and-push-broom neighbor drove by in his immaculately washed mid-90's pickup. He waved hello and I waved back. Either he hadn't seen me cavorting with his enemy or had decided he didn't care. That was the only other time I saw him. I kept his stuff for three days before putting it back behind his garage, and he never complained or came to find it. On my way out of town, I relayed my earlier conversation with him to my Mexican friend who owns the house. He was astonished, said the guy had always been nice to him and they had complained together about the folks across the street and even about the squatter who used to live there (and who continued to occasionally break in and did in fact still live off and on in the nearby woods). I guess that's America. Lucas PS As always, if there's someone you think might find this post or one of the other ones on this substack interesting, please share them! ## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| |
Standing Against the Radical Shift
.Recently, as highlighted in an article by The Hill, the resurfaced past comments of a far-left candidate underscore a **concerning and radical shift occurring within the Democrat Party.** For example, during a televised debate, progressive Michigan candidate Abdul El-Sayed had to defend past leaked comments where he suggested that progressives needed to rethink the way Americans celebrate Independence Day, suggesting the removal of fireworks. This is just one of several instances of controversial rhetoric from the far-left, including Francesca Hong—Democrat primary candidate for Wisconsin Governor—suggesting the cancellation of thanksgiving.
.This far-left shift is not just a national issue—it is actively harming families right here in Illinois' 6th Congressional District.
.Incumbent Democrat Sean Casten is part of this radical shift. Instead of focusing on policies that benefit the hardworking people of the 6th District, Congressman Casten is more concerned with messaging and satisfying the more radical elements of his party. For instance, **Casten recently refused to condemn socialism, voting against a U.S. House measure that would have done so.**
In stark contrast, **Niki Conforti maintains a "district-first" mentality** and is committed to delivering sensible solutions for her constituents. Niki will support legislation that benefits the 6th District, including:

* **Stimulating Economic Growth:** Niki will pass legislation that aims to stimulate economic growth and business activity. She will work to stimulate the return of manufacturing to the 6th District and provide relief by getting people back to work.
.
* **Job Creation:** In Congress, Niki will work to expand workforce training programs and help connect hard-working Illinoisans with good-paying jobs.
.
* **Improving Infrastructure & Stopping Tax Hikes:** We need infrastructure improvements, and Niki supports passing legislation for infrastructure funding—without stuffing the bill with special interest funding. She strongly opposes tax and fee hikes on Illinoisans and will work to curb the spending in Washington to stop tax increases on working families.
.
* **Lowering Energy and Healthcare Costs:** Niki will push for legislation that cuts regulations in the energy industry to make energy more resilient and more affordable. She will also tap into her professional expertise in the healthcare industry to push for legislation that increases transparency in medical billing, driving up competition in the healthcare marketplace to drive down prices for patients.

While her opponent caters to special interests and radical agendas, Niki Conforti will prioritize the voice of everyday citizens. It is time for sensible **solutions that protect your wallet and secure our nation's financial future.**
Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/FanlS7S_Ig2?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)

name: Molly Gray
subject: Five years since the fall of Kabul
body:
Dear Peter, Today marks five years since the fall of Kabul and the withdrawal of U.S. forces from Afghanistan. Over the past several years, I’ve had the privilege of working alongside Afghan allies who now call Vermont home. Many risked everything to support U.S. military and diplomatic missions in Afghanistan, including serving as interpreters for the Vermont National Guard and other branches of our military. Today, Afghan Vermonters are an important part of communities across our state. They are helping fill critical workforce needs in healthcare, manufacturing, human services, education, housing, and many other fields. They are building new lives here, raising families, and contributing to the communities we all call home. But for many, the story is far from over. Sadly, many Afghan families remain separated from loved ones, including wives and children still in hiding in Afghanistan. Others have endured years of immigration processing delays or, more recently, fear and uncertainty as a result of actions by the Trump Administration and ICE. For many in Vermont's Afghan community, today is an incredibly difficult day. I hope Vermonters will join me in offering our Afghan neighbors, friends, and colleagues the gratitude, compassion, and solidarity they deserve. And if you are able, please consider volunteering with or supporting [organizations](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137288540/640284148/1044169797?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZGNjMzMxMS1iYzk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5WqBzQD93s-R4k-AHdeIJHagi9NMvS6hncGDjm96Xrc=&emci=fca2e7d0-ba98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=2dcc3311-bc98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=43402276) working alongside Vermont's Afghan community. We have an obligation to stand with the people who stood with us. Five years later, that responsibility remains. With gratitude, _Molly Gray_ | | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137288541/640284149/679520187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZGNjMzMxMS1iYzk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5WqBzQD93s-R4k-AHdeIJHagi9NMvS6hncGDjm96Xrc=)

subject: We're already behind
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Democratic Party of Wisconsin, wisdems
body:
We need to catch up | | | | Derek, quick and urgent: I'm David Crowley, and I just became the Democratic nominee for Governor of Wisconsin. While I'm excited and ready for the challenge, I'm also nervous: **My opponent MAGA Tom Tiffany has already raised more than $15 million, including a $10 million transfer straight from the state Republican Party.** He ran basically unopposed for months. Voter registration is where elections are won or lost before a single vote is cast.
#
Peter,
**We are officially exactly one month away from National Voter Registration Day on September 15th, and we’re gearing up for our biggest voter registration push of the year.**
Preparing for a campaign of this scale requires building infrastructure and securing resources right now, long before September 15th arrives.
For years, MAGA Republicans have spent time and money trying to make it harder for Latino voters to register, harder to cast a ballot, and harder to make their voices heard.
National Voter Registration Day is our biggest opportunity to push back and prove that their suppression tactics will not stop Latino voters from showing up.
**To fund our voter registration drives between now and November, we’ve set an ambitious $50,000 goal to raise.**
It costs just $26 to register one voter. Every $26 contribution right now gives us the funds we need to run targeted digital outreach, organize in key communities, and make sure no Latino voter is left off the rolls.

Hey folks,
This one is personal.
I'm breaking down the ongoing investigation into my company by Trump's DOJ and the baseless right-wing conspiracy theory behind it. The legal bills. The threats. The toll on my family and my team. But I believe this is about something much bigger than me: using the power of government to intimidate people who speak out. And why I refuse to let any of it scare me into silence.
I have to be careful about what I say while this is ongoing. But I'm not going to be silent.

* [**00:04:11**] I explain the Laura Loomer conspiracy theory targeting me, how it escalated from internet attacks to a House Judiciary Committee subpoena, and why we fought back.
* [**00:07:35**] What I can--and can't--say about the ongoing investigation, plus the quote I gave to The New York Times about what I call a baseless "fishing expedition."

* [**00:12:34**] A personal message about my business, my staff, my family, and why none of this is going to grind me down.

This episode is about what happens when political intimidation stops being abstract and lands at your front door. It's about fear, power, accountability, and why we cannot allow threats and investigations to scare good people away from participating in our democracy. name: Thompson 4ND
subject: UPDATED CALL TO ACTION: Committee Agrees to Hear Data Center Proposals Monday
body:
CALL TO ACTION: Legislative Committee Agrees to Hear Data Center Proposals Monday
There is Still Time to Make Your Voice Heard Before Monday at Thompson4ND.com.

The North Dakota Legislative Management Committee meets Monday, August 17, at 10:00 a.m. in the Roughrider Room at the State Capitol in Bismarck.

We are asking for a one year moratorium on new permits so ordinances and laws catch up with the issues these facilities present. We are asking for a ban on government officials and signing non-disclosure agreements with data center developers.

The committee has agreed to consider Sen. Tim Mathern's two proposed bills and one resolution addressing data center development:
• Bill draft 25.1452.01000 - Moratorium on data centers - Senator Tim Mathern
• Bill draft 25.1425.01000 - Prohibiting nondisclosure agreements for data centers -
Senator Tim Mathern
• Resolution draft 25.3122.01000 - Study data centers - Senator Tim Mathern

**HERE 'S HOW YOU CAN TAKE ACTION:**
**1\. Contact your legislators.**
Go to Thompson4ND.com and use the link at the top of the homepage to contact your legislator directly about the upcoming Special Session.

**2\. Contact members of the Legislative Management Committee.**
If you cannot attend Monday's meeting in person, you can still make your voice heard. Photos and contact information for committee members are available in a link in the comment section so you can share your position on the proposed moratorium and NDA prohibition.

**3\. Share this information.**
Your voice matters—but so does the collective voice of North Dakotans.

Don't wait until after the decision is made. Make your voice heard before Monday’s meeting.
Please share this widely and encourage your family, friends, neighbors, farmers, ranchers, and communities to get involved.

This is your government. Your voice deserves to be heard.

Click on each of the 16 members' photos on the Legislative Management Committee to see phone numbers, email addresses, or both to contact them.

Vern

● Personal Message
---
Peter,
---

body:
Unable to help door knock, chip in to the campaign!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jonnyutah4congress/field-report-week-of-august-9th-16th-time-is-running-out-help-us-door-knock-10351357?e=c29ddb867a)

| | | | | |
# **Jonny’s Team Needs** _**YOU**_**🫵**
---
| | Hi Friend,
Scooby said it best, “ruh-roh!” We’re a little late in the weekly newsletter. We have had a lot of exciting things going on this week, and I am excited to share it all with you. We are going to need all hands on deck as we begin canvassing and going door to door. We will be asking for their support and vote. Mail-in ballots will be sent out in the next 60 days.
Our website shows the below counter now! We looked at getting billboards from now until election and we were quoted $20k!Please chip in and help me get these billboards to boost our name recognition in our ~22,000 square mile district. Your advocacy to your family, friends, neighbors and even co-workers to do the same goes a long way. There is no “I” in “Team”, and I cannot do this with you.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/YlObFOm3fpu?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=iz7H4aEOGnC-CHR2X6QVHCpigFapnZODV6b1Uj5A6w2AOD1okOWydEdXOCVf)
| [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/uUY4Ks0H0lu?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=ANB5x1fwOuerS-o5WesC17SnGtFs11_8NfDsy6Khn8EGyJXhspZScoBYn3ZZ)
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
