## Up Coming Next Couple Of Weeks
---
|
---
| |
#### **Come meet me in person**
_Check our Facebook events page for more info!_
Saturday, August 15th
* Sandy Day Of Action - _**11AM**_ @ Falcon Park, 9200 S 1700 E, Sandy - Come knock doors with us for a few hours
* One Community, One Ticket - Candidate Meet & Greet - _**1PM**_ @ Keller Williams, 4020 W Daybreak Parkway, South Jordan

Sunday, August 16th
* Dogs With Dems - Candidate Meet & Greet in the park, _**4PM**_ @ Sunnyside Park, 1735 Sunnyside Ave, Salt Lake City.

Monday, August 17th
* Utah County LDS Democrats Picnic Potluck, **6PM** @ Orem City Center Park, 300 E Center St, Orem.

Tuesday, August 25th
* Meet Congressional Candidate Jonny Larsen - Hosted by the Utah Democratic Senior Caucus - _**7PM**_ hosted [Via Zoom](https://us.list-manage.com/hJRarMABpeZ?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=30K5qCeAlKB2uDpDk3RjFf6oX03zFtYfcsjXl8jnQeeVww9PVCK6ZqDrV1Oz), more information here: [https://www.facebook.com/events/1863946444569452/](https://us.list-manage.com/NX55vFfjHuu?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=ALu6MV6fmuCHvJyymHOC5MJX9VfwqXFnwHuMLEbFVwNCGzJ-ezc4Y5kPUiEV)

Saturday, August 29th
* BBQ With Jonny - Place TBA, 4PM - 6PM. Mark your calendars, more information to come!

---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
## What we need & what we did this week
---
|
---
| |
### Volunteers
---
| | Working for a campaign is challenging. Even more so when you are donating your time.
We need to fill some specialty roles as well as have volunteers to accompany us for events, town halls, and canvassers to phone bank and door knock. This is an **ALL HANDS ON DECK** request!
Send an email to [Maria](mailto:volunteer@jonnyutah4congress.com?subject=Interested%20in%20volunteering%20for%20Jonny%20Larsen&body=Full%20name%2C%20phone%2C%20county%20and%20city%20you%20live%20in.%0A%0APlease%20share%20where%20you%20think%20you%20could%20best%20help%20volunteer%20for%20our%20campaign.%20No%20prior%20experience%20is%20needed%20but%20if%20you%20have%20it%2C%20please%20share!), our volunteer coordinator, to find out more.
---
|
---
| |
### Senator Cory Booker
---
| | Senator Cory Booker was in town and met with many Utah Democrats in Salt Lake and in Park City. I was fortunate enough to meet with him and share why we are a competitive district that would benefit from national party help!
Senator Booker shared inspiring stories that touched everyone who attended. What really stood out to me was his message of hope being a muscle. [Check out what he said by clicking here](https://us.list-manage.com/fP7z_Yu6nbv?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=BNK2s-DcIx1OD0XOLxEAj8mCA2wEAr-nr180paM9QjdZrp0QB1YwP48seWHX).
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/d4MTPMLDGvj?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=n9gsCB-BzzKkh9KdgCZA3xkIbiw1d65gRLb79QkjYm4fYAAlzD0yBzl87-Jz)
| |
### Q3 Meeting In Kane County
---
| | Huge shout out to Kane County Chair Caralee Woods for all the work that she and her amazing team put into hosting the Q3 central committee meeting in Kanab. [See a portion of my speech here](https://us.list-manage.com/aKOoMccBZMR?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=T7jsW1s3Srjx05D8jA7r2Bf2m8faHcexXAy-xccAbxrJkDX33uXRBtQcqMdg)
Chair Woods has been a huge supporter of ours for over a year since we first met in May of 2025 at Kane County Convention. I cannot express my gratitude enough for everything that she has done to support me and our campaign.
The food was absolutely amazing and I had a wonderful time. The drive down 89 to view the beautiful red rock is something everyone should experience at least once. If you have not been to Kanab, I highly recommend you go and visit.
---
| |
### Fire devistation continues
---
| | As of Friday, August 14th 2026, the Widemouth 2 fire has been 65% contained. On August 7th we lost two brave men who were instrumental in battling the fire in an unfortunate helicopter crash. Elliott from Porterville, CA and Andersen from Stateline, NV, we honor you for your bravery and dedication to safety of our community. You will not be forgotten, till Valhalla we met brothers. Semper Fi.
Fillmore and the surrounding areas are at high risk for burn scar flooding. As soon as I hear of the next sandbag filling event, I will let everyone know. Let’s show up as a community and help out our neighbors in a time of great need.
---
| |
### Fliers, Door Hangers, and Yard Signs
---
| | We have new fliers, new door hangers, and new yard signs! I had a unique request from a supporter and decided to print a few signs that welcome anyone who might be feeling politically homeless. We have “Republicans For” and “Independents For” yard signs in limited quantities. If you know anyone who is interested in one, invite them to one of our events above so they can come pick one up.
You can find all the canvassing events, door knocking, training, and more at the Utah Democrats mobilize page. [https://www.mobilize.us/utahdemocrats/](https://us.list-manage.com/7qPlUWKT_9d?e=c29ddb867a&c2id=ae2ec488ed0a92b1bb8171b838f89423&m=ZggNK7RZqlaSd8JI0Xxpi065zhc9bupQFBmt3Ue_bxIUd6hsgbcw9NfGTGCi)
---
|
---
| |
If you want to volunteer or know people who do, please click and share the volunteer/newsletter sign up page below. We are always in need of donations. Click and share the link with your family, friends, neighbors, and coworkers.
---

subject: Democrats haven’t held a majority in the Pennsylvania State Senate in nearly 50 years. Let’s change that.

body:
Winning a Democratic trifecta in this critical swing state would be a game-changer heading into the 2028 presidential election.
#
Hi there,
Democrats in Pennsylvania haven’t had a majority in the State Senate _for almost 50 years_. Republicans have maintained a tight grip on the chamber since 1978, but this year, voters have a chance to change that.
Democratic Governor Josh Shapiro is heavily favored to win re-election, and his momentum can help Democrats widen their one-seat majority in the State House and flip the State Senate. If they do, they’ll secure a trifecta in one of the nation’s most important swing states. That’s why this year, Swing Left is going all in on these state-level races in Pennsylvania to make it happen.
**We have two clear objectives here: Democrats need to flip just 3 seats in the State Senate, and protect (or even expand) their majority in the State House to secure a trifecta.**
[****](https://act.swingleft.org/go/66?c0=sl-states-pa-2026.46fXcv&refcode=em20260815-2457&t=1&akid=2457%2E1562180%2E16wSaL)
[****](https://act.swingleft.org/go/66?c0=sl-states-pa-2026.46fXcv&refcode=em20260815-2457&t=2&akid=2457%2E1562180%2E16wSaL)
Winning a Democratic trifecta in this critical swing state would be a game-changer heading into the 2028 presidential election, unlocking transformative policy progress for millions of Pennsylvanians, allowing Democrats to pass a long-overdue minimum wage increase, codify abortion rights into law, lower utility costs, and build more affordable housing without obstruction from the right. It would also block Republicans from restricting voting rights or gerrymandering Pennsylvania’s congressional maps ahead of the next election.
Control of both chambers will hinge on a few ultra-competitive swing districts, including several in suburban Philadelphia and southeastern Pennsylvania. So in order to help Democrats win in the closest races, **we’re directing grassroots funds straight to Pennsylvania’s Democratic legislative caucus committees.**
Caucus committees focus fully on winning the State House and State Senate. Your support will go directly into the campaigns in the toss-up districts that will decide majority control.
[**If you’re ready to support these critical state-level races in Pennsylvania, will you make a donation of $25 to our Pennsylvania Win in the States Fund today to help hold the State House and flip the State Senate?**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-pa-2026.9BSmNP&refcode=em20260815-2457&amount=25&t=3&akid=2457%2E1562180%2E16wSaL)
**[Donate $25 Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-pa-2026.9BSmNP&refcode=em20260815-2457&amount=25&t=4&akid=2457%2E1562180%2E16wSaL)**
Thank you for being part of this work.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137300897/640309332/-1099661026?refcode=260815-underdog&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MDZjZDJiZi1jYTk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ULQgC4AXZv4Z5ml_XDuGIwalWR6rsT4JhPa9xgBE7Lk=)

As a child with severe chronic asthma, I was constantly told what I wouldn’t be able to do. _And I proved them wrong._
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137300898/640309333/-1099661026?refcode=260815-underdog&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MDZjZDJiZi1jYTk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ULQgC4AXZv4Z5ml_XDuGIwalWR6rsT4JhPa9xgBE7Lk=)
---
When I first ran for school board in 2004, I was up against a crowded field — including two incumbents — and people told me I had no chance of winning. I became the youngest person to be elected to the Minneapolis Board of Education and won the most votes. _I proved the doubters wrong._
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137300899/640309334/-1099661026?refcode=260815-underdog&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MDZjZDJiZi1jYTk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ULQgC4AXZv4Z5ml_XDuGIwalWR6rsT4JhPa9xgBE7Lk=)
---
In 2015, I became only the second Native American woman in the Minnesota House when I won my special election and _proved the doubters wrong_. I'm the daughter of Hmong refugees. My parents fled the CIA's secret war in Laos and came to California with the hope that their children might have opportunities they never had.

I grew up in South Sacramento as the oldest of 16 kids. Responsibility wasn't something I learned later in life. I helped raise my siblings. I translated for my parents. I showed up when my community needed me.

When our neighborhood schools faced closure, I co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics to give families like mine a voice. When immigrant families were under attack, I passed California's first Safe Haven Resolution as a school board member.

When something isn't right, I don't sit quietly and hope it changes. I step up. That's why I'm running for Congress.

Too many of the people making decisions for working families in Washington have never lived what those families are going through. They've never translated a document for a parent, never stretched a paycheck to the end of the month, never watched their community get treated like an afterthought.

I have. That's not a talking point — it's my whole life. And it's exactly the perspective this seat has been missing.

clean_body: My parents fled the CIA's secret war in Laos | | | | Team, I'm the daughter of Hmong refugees. My parents fled the CIA's secret war in Laos and came to California with the hope that their children might have opportunities they never had. I grew up in South Sacramento as the oldest of 16 kids. Responsibility wasn't something I learned later in life. I helped raise my siblings. I translated for my parents. I showed up when my community needed me. When our neighborhood schools faced closure, I co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics to give families like mine a voice. When immigrant families were under attack, I passed California's first Safe Haven Resolution as a school board member. When something isn't right, I don't sit quietly and hope it changes. I step up. That's why I'm running for Congress. Too many of the people making decisions for working families in Washington have never lived what those families are going through. They've never translated a document for a parent, never stretched a paycheck to the end of the month, never watched their community get treated like an afterthought. I have. That's not a talking point — it's my whole life. And it's exactly the perspective this seat has been missing. | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | With heart and hustle, Mai | Mai is the daughter of Hmong refugees, born and raised in Sacramento. Mai’s parents fled war in Laos and arrived in California to find a new life. As the oldest of 16 children, she helped raise her siblings while working hard to build a career dedicated to helping her community thrive. Mai is a proud product of public schools and was the first in her family to attend college. As a young organizer, Mai returned home to serve the community that raised and supported her. [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260815_1_ak.DqX4WY&amount=5&refcode=em20260815-683&t=3&akid=692%2E127862%2E3JYag8)
ICYMI, MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo got pulled over, and instantly tried using his name to get out of a ticket.
We keep thinking about this moment, because it really sums up how Lombardo operates. **Lombardo thinks the rules are for everybody else — and Nevada families are the ones who end up paying for it, over and over:**
* Lombardo fired Nevada’s top water regulator after mining companies complained, then took **$500k** from one of the companies months later.
* On top of that, he vetoed a bipartisan bill that would've lowered prescription drug costs, then banked over **$80k** from the groups that opposed it.

The traffic stop wasn’t a one-time mishap. This is who Lombardo is at his core, and we need to make sure every Nevadan knows it before they head to the polls in November.

The Global War on Terror Memorial Foundation **[revealed the design plans](https://substack.com/redirect/994b83fd-5eb1-45f0-bc0b-d418aec3534a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for the Global War on Terror (GWOT) memorial that is slated to be built on the National Mall in Washington, DC. Designed by Japanese architect Kengo Kuma, the plan garnered a swift--and brutal--reaction online. Veterans of the (GWOT) ranging from **[top lawmakers](https://substack.com/redirect/34a76d43-2ad0-42ea-ada7-dea6ec6a63c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to **[regular troops](https://substack.com/redirect/36423da6-9bae-4880-9daa-722f2ad87ed9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** made their voices heard, expressing their dissatisfaction and disappointment with the current plan. Many demanded that the Foundation go back to the drawing board and come up with something better. Even the founder of the Global War on Terror Memorial Foundation, Andrew J. Brennan, spoke out in an **[opinion piece published on](https://substack.com/redirect/14a9809b-df52-4986-bf29-637a1ce1d05b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** _**[Military Times](https://substack.com/redirect/14a9809b-df52-4986-bf29-637a1ce1d05b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ calling for a new design and new leadership for the Foundation.
**I share their disappointment.**
I served for 9 years as an infantryman in the Army National Guard, from 2003-2012. During that time, I was called up for two deployments in support of GWOT: first, in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba and then in Iraq. When I heard that there were plans in the works to place a memorial to GWOT on the National Mall, I was cautiously optimistic that it could be made in such a way that it would truly honor the service and sacrifices of those who answered the call to duty.
**This design fails to do so.**

In the first place, it is unintelligible. The function of a memorial (from the Latin _memoria_) is to bring to mind something in order to encourage reflection. Hence, memorials should be clear in their meaning to allow the thing memorialized to be easily and readily brought to mind. This means they should not require extensive explanation to be understood: explanation interferes with the immediacy of the experience. This design fails at that basic task.
But secondly, and more fundamentally, it fails because it seems to forget what it _is_. **This is not just a memorial but a** _**war memorial.**_
The nature of war--involving, as it does, conflict, destruction, injury, and death--is such that it is inevitably tragic. Though the human condition is such that it is often necessary to engage in warfare, these aspects of war mean that it should be avoided whenever possible.
And yet, terrible as it is, war also enables a kind of human greatness. Many of the greatest human actions that punctuate human history would not have been possible in the absence of war. In his _Nicomachean Ethics_ , Aristotle highlights the virtue of courage as that which is most characteristically displayed on the battlefield.
Though courage as turns out to be the lowest in the taxonomy of virtue for Aristotle--and even if, as Cicero reminds us, we can speak (analogously) of courage in other contexts--courage nevertheless serves to begin the movement toward higher virtues. If this is true, then it would seem to imply that there is something intrinsic to human nature that looks to war as a kind of elevation of itself.

Consider that many of the greatest works of literature and art--from the _Iliad_ to the Bayeux Tapestry to the _Song of Roland_ to the _Charge of the Light Brigade_ to _Saving Private Ryan_ --take war as their subject, in order to highlight the great acts of courage, commitment, patriotism, and sacrifice made possible only in the crucible of war.
Of course, war is violent and therefore it does leave wounds--physical, mental, and emotional--on those individuals who participate in them. And, for those who never return, it leaves scars on families, communities--vacancies that can never be filled. These wounds do require healing, and there is a need spaces that encourage reflection and healing are important. But as important as reflection and healing are, _**this is not the primary task of a war**_****_**memorial.**_
This is for two reasons.
**First,** since the trauma of loss is an intrinsic part of the human condition, it is _not_ unique to the experience of war. If memorials are simply about healing from traumatic experiences, why single out wars to memorialize and leave aside the countless other human experiences in which trauma of loss is present. The reason for building war memorials is to commemorate what is unique about war--of which, the wounding and loss is only a part. The reason for building war memorials, in other words, is _first_ to encourage reflection on the virtues that war enables and the sacrifices it entails, and only secondarily for therapeutic purposes (if at all).
**Second,** war memorials serve an inherently _public_ function: they act as permanent reminders of the war in public space. This is _particularly_ true of those on the National Mall. Their public function is to encourage remembrance by future generations of the sacrifices made by earlier generations. In this way, they foster filial piety and gratitude. When a memorial is conflated with a therapeutic exercise, on the other hand, the memorial trends to lose meaning with the passage of time as those of the generation who endured that trauma pass on.

Fortunately, there are models that we can look toward for inspiration. The recently opened World War I memorial, located just off the National Mall at Pershing Park, is an excellent example of a memorial that encourages remembrances of courage and sacrifice. Its stunning _bas relief_ , designed by sculptor Sabin Howard and entitled _[A](https://substack.com/redirect/c615e2b7-8927-46d8-bd3c-2dee94c4b366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Soldier's Journey](https://substack.com/redirect/c615e2b7-8927-46d8-bd3c-2dee94c4b366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_, echoes the Campbellian "hero's journey" motif. Yet, it is not simply jingoistic. It does not shy away from depicting the hardship and tragedy of war, but neither does it wallow in it. It perfectly captures both the heroism _and_ the horror of war--and the burdens borne by those who participate in the fighting, as well as those who are left behind.
One suspects that this was made possible by the fact there are no living veterans of that war, and, in that sense, there was no temptation toward the therapeutic. In this sense, the task of a war memorial was far clearer in that case: inspiring remembrance for future generations. We can, and should, learn from this model. By asking **" what will this monument mean once all those who served or lost someone in this war are gone?"** we can more clearly recognize the proper task of a war memorial: public _anamnesis_ for the preservation of cultural memory and the recognition of the greatness that is paradoxically enabled only by the tragedy of war.

The reason for building war memorials, in other words, is first to encourage reflection on the virtues that war enables and the sacrifices it entails, and only secondarily for therapeutic purposes (if at all). Second, war memorials serve an inherently public function: they act as permanent reminders of the war in public space. This is particularly true of those on the National Mall. Their public function is to encourage remembrance by future generations of the sacrifices made by earlier generations. In this way, they foster filial piety and gratitude. When a memorial is conflated with a therapeutic exercise, on the other hand, the memorial trends to lose meaning with the passage of time as those of the generation who endured that trauma pass on. Fortunately, there are models that we can look toward for inspiration. The recently opened World War I memorial, located just off the National Mall at Pershing Park, is an excellent example of a memorial that encourages remembrances of courage and sacrifice. Its stunning bas relief , designed by sculptor Sabin Howard and entitled , echoes the Campbellian "hero's journey" motif. Yet, it is not simply jingoistic. It does not shy away from depicting the hardship and tragedy of war, but neither does it wallow in it. It perfectly captures both the heroism and the horror of war--and the burdens borne by those who participate in the fighting, as well as those who are left behind. One suspects that this was made possible by the fact there are no living veterans of that war, and, in that sense, there was no temptation toward the therapeutic. In this sense, the task of a war memorial was far clearer in that case: inspiring remembrance for future generations. We can, and should, learn from this model. By asking " what will this monument mean once all those who served or lost someone in this war are gone?" we can more clearly recognize the proper task of a war memorial: public anamnesis for the preservation of cultural memory and the recognition of the greatness that is paradoxically enabled only by the tragedy of war. Shaun Rieley is Director of Educational Programs and Teaching Fellow at Hillsdale College 's Washington, DC Campus. Let us know your thoughts. * You're currently a free subscriber to . | | Dear Peter,
Our campaign was by far the strongest ever by an openly Marxist candidate for the U.S. Congress.
We've won a historic 17.3 percent of the vote in a five-way race, in Washington’s sprawling Ninth Congressional District. Nearly 24,500 people voted for a Marxist in the district, which spans suburban areas with a significant proportion of Republican voters in addition to large parts of the major urban areas of Seattle and Bellevue.
This is an incredible result! We need to use this to continue building movements that confront the Democratic and Republican parties, both of which represent the war-profiteering billionaires and multimillionaires.
We ran on electrifying demands like free healthcare for all funded by taxing the rich, ending all military aid to Israel and a permanent arms embargo on Israel, and national rent control. All of these are extremely popular among the working class in this district and nationally.
We achieved this result despite the many obstacles we faced.
Both the Republican and Democratic parties maneuvered by running candidates specifically to block our campaign from getting into the November election, which would have resulted in a head-to-head battle between our campaign and genocidal Democrat Adam Smith.
We faced a corporate media blackout and hostility and outright attacks from DSA leaders and many "progressive" podcasters.
Many labor leaders shamelessly endorsed Adam Smith, while others remained silent, effectively supporting Smith.
All of these obstacles were predictable. Our decade on the Seattle City Council showed what a threat we are to the political establishment and those who give them cover. We used our decade on the Seattle City Council to relentlessly build working-class movements, winning four elections and unparalleled victories such as the nation's highest minimum wage, which also led to substantive raises for tens of millions of workers across the United States, defeating Jeff Bezos to win the Amazon Tax, and repeatedly beating corporate landlords to win unprecedented renters' rights.
Despite not making it into the November election, we've provided a powerful example of what's possible by running an openly Marxist independent campaign based on class struggle rather than making peace with the political establishment or its legions of gatekeepers.
The DSA strategy of appeasing and, worse, rehabilitating the discredited Democratic leadership and their rotten party is a dead end. In this age of imperialist war and climate catastrophe, we simply have no time to fuck around.
We urgently need militant movements of the working class and a new mass party that can defeat the billionaires and both their parties. And we need revolutionary socialist campaigns like mine that don’t try to join the establishment and help administer the capitalist system, but are fighting to overthrow it.
Solidarity,
Kshama Sawant

name: OnePA Team
subject: No parent should have to choose between a baby and a paycheck
body:
Working people are organizing for something families in nearly every other country already have. | |
---
Peter, **Right now, we’re organizing alongside workers, nurses, parents, and community leaders to win paid parental leave in Allegheny County.** Families should have time to recover from childbirth, bond with a new baby, and care for the people they love without wondering how they are going to make rent or keep food on the table. **But working people should not have to organize county by county just to win time to care for a new child.** Out of 195 nations around the world, all but 9 provide paid parental leave. The United States is one of those 9. Instead, we have a patchwork where some states have stepped up, but 36 states, including Pennsylvania, offer no statewide paid leave program at all. The current federal law is not enough. Eligible workers can receive up to 12 weeks of family and medical leave, but it is *unpaid.* For a family living paycheck to paycheck, the “right” to take weeks away from work without income is not much of a right. It means too many parents are pushed back to work before they have healed, before they have had time to bond with their baby, and simply because the bills will not wait. That burden falls hardest on working people who already have the least economic security. Lower-wage workers and people of color are less likely to have access to paid leave. In Allegheny County, severe maternal morbidity rose 55% between 2016 and 2022, and Black infants are more than twice as likely to die as white infants.**National paid leave is one concrete way to give families more time, security, and support during a critical moment.** [**We’re building power locally, and now we need to take that pressure to Washington. Tell Congress to guarantee paid parental leave for working families nationwide.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxitT1F9zF8z0XeYL16ZhMWrgK1AzA41kpG2x81tEWsQTMzx1ITbyfuYp7GgZ72u1Rr4X38e7P7afCzqHKRuZh2j1siiKfBFMArNhzKccZ6psymNqMj1M6a2Gl4yiE7_2Ks9eIO782cFJAEYLbR1g1-WdUlSUNlobu-AWGSD43In06CkuhSt0EtZl0HBPZ7OdXt4VZs-2wTmC0f0RbRr0LDmVgoLzTQtevZx_Z_CKXKQjmrLDpY30NPIh-CnFCcQ4Bro1QSkcvawzbJzIIkrWtBj3HK0mIPsQUbzM3tnGf3m_fJHfkZjYCNwH0aPNTbaOzewdJ-1NQ0Ttbrit0GAUv51HeSZlsFrHhzefESM73ThM/4t7/jjM0Wzb1TKu4RWIwbfotHg/h0/h001.gDsfjCOUGvJUv1efs7zNr5ZsxT4DQgKw0exKlYszC-8) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxitT1F9zF8z0XeYL16ZhMWrgK1AzA41kpG2x81tEWsQQtpOQHNCVcXP-H6LchI7hpWxrgeLPZzqmrNa2k_aFynbp8d1bUvxioS7tjzrKm9du0INyQZbCht5sEOXTAiZKZ4mnjeg3mP-QYwMqEoPWlcp_zDIBCbZ59Dvji3EEN7lu0tycR2Iwu5ddo8C6rzKGwUjjHdiOJSMbc6EYPuDXK4HZMRu4IdJYMAksOUvQQkNyLglH4EHR9loA8JCnXnYajeIVW3VdyOBQ8sCF3P3Ha27koQF1Q-FZzGW9nrZn-4s8Rs4dgXLy_38AE8AoBvvl_WPUMkGak4QzO1Rq_tiQGceFrULDFiN9r_Gn6T5VtmGQ/4t7/jjM0Wzb1TKu4RWIwbfotHg/h1/h001.H6EUzfNMGcH_eRY8qhJ1XQWy3P1GZJT1VxH3H3xApww)
---
**The organizing happening in Allegheny County shows what working people can do when we come together and demand more.** A broad coalition has pushed paid parental leave onto the public agenda because families are tired of being told that caring for a newborn is a private problem they should somehow solve on their own.
And this is not just good for families. Paid leave helps people stay in the workforce, supports recruitment and retention, and can reduce turnover. It gives working people a little more stability at a moment when too many families are already struggling with rising costs.
We will keep fighting in Allegheny County. We will keep building toward statewide paid leave in Pennsylvania. But our movement should not have to recreate this fight in thousands of counties and dozens of state legislatures while Congress sits on its hands.
**Working people are organizing because we know families deserve better. If enough of us build pressure from our neighborhoods all the way to Washington, we can turn paid parental leave from a benefit some employers choose to provide into a basic protection every family can count on.**
[**Tell Congress to pass national paid parental leave and give every working family the time and financial security to care for a new child.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxitT1F9zF8z0XeYL16ZhMWrgK1AzA41kpG2x81tEWsQThvVo6JQ58d9_ZSNL4CjMhxjdVa2sy9cirPav0ImBeorSHZwxGU1xcXzqPcwUHSuKUYOGlvVFvTtnQxV5CGs028ldy5rwl4xQbGNg_NkFCH3Wd2QedDCoN7quZnIvYHh8IuPPuZIGn2WjBTTvypqju8puhf-_gTYyaudkWT6omorZo_fx_otNkw7eEp03pKwb47lvIz-InWhgW4F5VYPqC5FTwDc3VRj0iI4WJpCAJKgQDaR1Z5JGzFs6GWy-IqiFIYQ0girygxDmH2gqQQ0WuXGr0js2-8ktINXUpMhIiWAoifaf0IInt6SAh5Yjgg2c/4t7/jjM0Wzb1TKu4RWIwbfotHg/h2/h001.HkaeMru-OjW_Q63vXVIbbvXhxEOoUwu5I7zY4JCdpRk)
Together, let’s win paid leave for every family.

clean_body: Working people are organizing for something families in nearly every other country already have. | | Peter, Right now, we’re organizing alongside workers, nurses, parents, and community leaders to win paid parental leave in Allegheny County. Families should have time to recover from childbirth, bond with a new baby, and care for the people they love without wondering how they are going to make rent or keep food on the table. But working people should not have to organize county by county just to win time to care for a new child. Out of 195 nations around the world, all but 9 provide paid parental leave. The United States is one of those 9. Instead, we have a patchwork where some states have stepped up, but 36 states, including Pennsylvania, offer no statewide paid leave program at all. The current federal law is not enough. Eligible workers can receive up to 12 weeks of family and medical leave, but it is unpaid. For a family living paycheck to paycheck, the “right” to take weeks away from work without income is not much of a right. It means too many parents are pushed back to work before they have healed, before they have had time to bond with their baby, and simply because the bills will not wait. That burden falls hardest on working people who already have the least economic security. Lower-wage workers and people of color are less likely to have access to paid leave. In Allegheny County, severe maternal morbidity rose 55% between 2016 and 2022, and Black infants are more than twice as likely to die as white infants.National paid leave is one concrete way to give families more time, security, and support during a critical moment. | | The organizing happening in Allegheny County shows what working people can do when we come together and demand more. A broad coalition has pushed paid parental leave onto the public agenda because families are tired of being told that caring for a newborn is a private problem they should somehow solve on their own. And this is not just good for families. Paid leave helps people stay in the workforce, supports recruitment and retention, and can reduce turnover. It gives working people a little more stability at a moment when too many families are already struggling with rising costs. We will keep fighting in Allegheny County. We will keep building toward statewide paid leave in Pennsylvania. But our movement should not have to recreate this fight in thousands of counties and dozens of state legislatures while Congress sits on its hands. Working people are organizing because we know families deserve better. If enough of us build pressure from our neighborhoods all the way to Washington, we can turn paid parental leave from a benefit some employers choose to provide into a basic protection every family can count on. Together, let’s win paid leave for every family. -OnePA | OnePA is a 501(c)4 organization Contributions to OnePA are not tax deductible for federal income tax purposes Our mailing address is P.O. I wouldn't trade a single moment of that service - the good, the bad, even the painful - because it shaped who I am. It gave me confidence, resilience, and a deep respect for every man and woman who wears the uniform.That's why I'm proud to stand with the American Veterans Center (AVC).**Their mission is simple but urgent: preserve the firsthand stories of America 's heroes, guarding their legacy and honoring their sacrifice, before they're gone forever.** In fact, this year will be my eighth year hosting their televised event, _American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes_ in November.But I'm writing to you today because every day, more veterans of World War II, Korea, and Vietnam pass on.When they do, their voices and their stories of courage, sacrifice, and grit risk being lost to time._Unless we act now_.**[Will you make your first gift today of $25, $50, $100, or any amount you can chip in to help preserve the stories of America’s veterans?](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=d62f2462f89747f0a7090f2792c7af59&_e=uL_d8FWqGAEa1MO2UL7PG5tMAN-roQ1IvVv8I8Gvdc7F9kZB2txmeEg3dGHvdalzUBvK2zCXHdFaso41pSg6ktALwRiO0KimPE-5juZmigGW95Az-nW7ZV0sS-dGu-69jlplwmyRzvxcnXune_hRPETB2yNNtH1fDnNvlIr2Xt_-qojzZyRcqWqT-DxzY01hWpvwDdMiGVYi2BIeY1PvUUSVf2irv1zSyIDhs5WlygPNlT8z8i8Aq2AzOZX2j8FFxR9bWIqUfKYEKbEVxn2t4W941WSpxYogh05B4EiL8zfZnU6ZmQpBOaolD-GxF9LktWoj72yYy1Uacf6HI5xWPR-rfEMe1vZUmI7ENaHBfcAc-M3Ktrh1HfrMKuy-i9sxrvvSi5FHxImlISP9Wgw2wGORwCxcz4xQwOHQLZ_vCyRbqGI3ahiyArQMB2hiOIomhUd-3NxJgIZSg8BLqvPZ_sLKR4jehr_fsg6B74CgPX4vNinfejwXo0Z8j3jSwM8OLchKDuVuIZn92IafBLdrRE9Cx07FtWZU6aADDxhGa73ytq3CUWlM5eWypJ6AGj2DKW3O9CSM7k04Q5oSYYBrOpBNo253cy6BjOJ3l1uNrSAYF9ShAeN-XkA6KXgQ1deDlNNZ9vSHR0khtxwDYoU14vuEeZE2MEILbdpMxvRJ_fG6W-vKB-uOzhgVuMMwo1lXmQRB9VQQh_wIMVKS5FViuq4Q1gtMY2R2teCBfrd7SRwqONU2FhO9Ct_2ZyrP5Or3)**

Fellow Patriot, here's something you should know: AVC doesn't take a single dollar of government funding. **Every documentary, every oral history, every story we preserve exists because of patriotic citizens like you.** And AVC has the track record to prove it. Recently they recorded several World War II veterans who shared about fighting in the Pacific theater, including:
* **Bob Wilson, 105, who enlisted in the Navy shortly after Pearl Harbor. **Just three years later, he took part in the D-Day landings at Normandy. Bob was awarded the French Legion of Honor in May 2025 for his valor.

* **Roberta "Randy" Tidmore, 103, a trailblazer in the U.S. Marine Corps Women 's Reserve.** Randy was a Rosie the Riveter who later served as president of the Women's Marine Association, advocating for the recognition of women's contributions in wartime.

* **Calvin Shiner, 102** , who served in an all-Black engineering battalion -- building bridges, repairing roads, and helping hold the line across Europe.

Right now, AVC is preparing to film several helicopter pilots who flew dangerous missions in Vietnam, as well as members of the legendary Night Stalkers. In November, they're hoping to sit down with many of the World War II veterans attending AVC's annual conference, heroes like:
* **Milton Ripple,** a U.S. Navy veteran of USS Pollux, operating throughout the Pacific Theater...

* **Dominick Critelli,** who served with the 95th Infantry Division, landing on Utah Beach on June 12, 1944...

* **Robert Boeke** , a veteran of the U.S. Army's 341st Infantry Regiment of the 86th Infantry Division who took part in the liberation of the infamous concentration camp at Dachau.

And this work is in addition to reviving and hosting our nation's largest Memorial Day event - the National Memorial Day Parade, which draws more than 300,000 spectators to Washington, DC in salute of our nation's fallen heroes! **I can personally vouch for AVC 's work, Fellow Patriot.** I've been the subject of two of their documentaries myself, and I know firsthand how seriously their small but mighty staff take the responsibility of capturing a veteran's story.

clean_body: Don’t let these stories disappear AVC preserves veterans' voices through powerful documentaries--but only with your help. | | | | Fellow Patriot, I'm Rob Riggle. Some folks know me from 12 Strong , Step Brothers , The Hangover , 21 Jump Street , and other movies. But before Hollywood, I spent 23 years serving in the United States Marine Corps. - Above: Rob Riggle and Edward Shames, veteran of the 101st Airborne and the last living officer from the famed 'Band of Brothers.' I wouldn't trade a single moment of that service - the good, the bad, even the painful - because it shaped who I am. It gave me confidence, resilience, and a deep respect for every man and woman who wears the uniform.That's why I'm proud to stand with the American Veterans Center (AVC).Their mission is simple but urgent: preserve the firsthand stories of America 's heroes, guarding their legacy and honoring their sacrifice, before they're gone forever. In fact, this year will be my eighth year hosting their televised event, American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes in November.But I'm writing to you today because every day, more veterans of World War II, Korea, and Vietnam pass on.When they do, their voices and their stories of courage, sacrifice, and grit risk being lost to time.Unless we act now. Fellow Patriot, here's something you should know: AVC doesn't take a single dollar of government funding. Every documentary, every oral history, every story we preserve exists because of patriotic citizens like you. And AVC has the track record to prove it. Recently they recorded several World War II veterans who shared about fighting in the Pacific theater, including: Bob Wilson, 105, who enlisted in the Navy shortly after Pearl Harbor. Just three years later, he took part in the D-Day landings at Normandy. Bob was awarded the French Legion of Honor in May 2025 for his valor. Roberta "Randy" Tidmore, 103, a trailblazer in the U.S. Marine Corps Women 's Reserve. Randy was a Rosie the Riveter who later served as president of the Women's Marine Association, advocating for the recognition of women's contributions in wartime. Calvin Shiner, 102 , who served in an all-Black engineering battalion -- building bridges, repairing roads, and helping hold the line across Europe. Right now, AVC is preparing to film several helicopter pilots who flew dangerous missions in Vietnam, as well as members of the legendary Night Stalkers. In November, they're hoping to sit down with many of the World War II veterans attending AVC's annual conference, heroes like: Milton Ripple, a U.S. Navy veteran of USS Pollux, operating throughout the Pacific Theater... Dominick Critelli, who served with the 95th Infantry Division, landing on Utah Beach on June 12, 1944... Robert Boeke , a veteran of the U.S. Army's 341st Infantry Regiment of the 86th Infantry Division who took part in the liberation of the infamous concentration camp at Dachau. And this work is in addition to reviving and hosting our nation's largest Memorial Day event - the National Memorial Day Parade, which draws more than 300,000 spectators to Washington, DC in salute of our nation's fallen heroes! I can personally vouch for AVC 's work, Fellow Patriot. I've been the subject of two of their documentaries myself, and I know firsthand how seriously their small but mighty staff take the responsibility of capturing a veteran's story. You see, they don't just point a camera and click "record" without a thought. They honor your service...they listen...and they preserve your story with care so it can inspire generations to come. Fellow Patriot, during my years of service, I was deployed to Libya to help evacuate the embassy.I was among the bucket brigades at Ground Zero after September 11th. I did two tours in Afghanistan, and in 2013, I retired as a lieutenant colonel. While I retired my uniform, giving back to those who served -- and ensuring these men and women feel supported, heard, and celebrated for their sacrifices -- is a key part of my life.As long as I'm alive, I'll be proud to have earned the title, "Marine," and I will feel loyal not only to other Marines but to all Americans who've served our nation. Above: Rob Riggle and Dick Cole, veteran of WWII and Jimmy Doolittle 's co-pilot on the Doolittle Raid. Fellow Patriot, AVC does tremendous work honoring the legacies of veterans through their Oral History Documentary program from all branches of service. These brave individuals selflessly risked their lives to safeguard our freedom. It's up to us to honor their unwavering dedication and ensure that their legacy of sacrifice is forever remembered and held in the highest esteem. Fellow Patriot, I 'll be honest--without you, these legacies may vanish. With you, they'll live on to inspire millions.Our veterans stood up for us. Now it's our turn to step up for them.Thank you for honoring their service by helping us tell their stories.Semper Fi, Rob Riggle on behalf of American Veterans Center United States Marine Corps (Ret.) The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. A non-profit educational organization, the AVC and WWIIVC are funded solely through generous contributions from people like you. All contributions are tax-deductible. Friend,

Having taught college students myself, I know how much trust, effort, and stability it takes to run a classroom. Our public universities exist to educate our kids, drive groundbreaking research, and employ dedicated educators.

When federal agents act with this kind of reckless overreach, it doesn't make anyone safer. It creates panic, disrupts students' education, and wastes resources that ought to be going toward real public safety threats.

Federal agencies should focus on real security threats, not on pulling teachers out of local classrooms. The Just The Truth TeamFriend, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life — a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Friend, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most — away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought — on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change — and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. Dear Friend, It was a big week!The **Minnesota Freedom Caucus** ran the table on Tuesday night and sent a message that ought to be heard in all 50 states.We've also got a Wyoming showdown big enough to pull in the _New York Times_ , a West Virginia fight over government surveillance, and a couple of wins worth celebrating in Louisiana and Missouri. Let's get into it.
---
|
---
**MINNESOTA** This is what the model looks like when it works. On Tuesday night, every member of your **Minnesota Freedom Caucus** who was on the ballot won their primary. All NINE. From Chairman Eric Lucero on down, the whole roster is headed to November with a win at their back. The Establishment did not want this. Swamp-backed candidates ran hard to override the party's own endorsements and shove the grassroots aside. They spent the money. They made the calls. And Minnesota Republicans looked at a group of members who never once hid who they are - who stood up a brand-new Freedom Caucus back in February and told the whole state exactly what they believe - and sent every one of them right back to St. Paul. Nine members ran as exactly who they are, and nine members are moving on. "You proved them wrong," the caucus told its supporters the next morning. Bravo to every one of them.
---
[](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjja-2FX-2BHiJMkQeHavsUeprX80ibB6obPhLBMdbCybdkNdj23fvbBzYuTOZ05LySEnEYA41d8xScx1YSvrPqloiFU-3DmANP_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAAxfrP2EcKHvUfAzofvDI0XLQ4VwSQibmBDGU8svUEkg5qJsA6C3xXBaAUcZCIEW2Q-2BexpRIFr0-2BQIL-2F2DwZdKGdG-2BWrRWDGdQ02hc8kOHepXysdwb37C6SqC1nTx99n0dK12nuBzSx6LDov3Unu9TXRi1EzdA-2Bi7yaiH7S99fPWhH8GTxEcHq9y7XvlGzMn2ip6UFGsNTVGZaDn9SNLrBoJkQqU-2FhiD3Uw9UICrco0-3D)
---
|
---
**WYOMING** The _New York Times_ just sent reporters all the way to Wyoming to write about your **Wyoming Freedom Caucus** \- the first Freedom Caucus in the country to take control of a statehouse chamber. Even the _Times_ had to admit that part.Then they blew the rest. The paper painted the caucus as "far right" and cast State Senator Ogden Driskill, the man running against them, as "merely right." So let's go to the tape. Our friends at the [Institute for Legislative Analysis](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjmY2AIel-2BnWqkMPNGZPnZyXyL-2FJeb5ou-2Fau1v-2BJi-2FhxWrbXcfiyJsADgnw0SYADnjqOLAA2hbN6q285C31eq2c0-3DGCHG_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerAAxfrP2EcKHvUfAzofvDI0XLQ4VwSQibmBDGU8svUEkg5qJsA6C3xXBaAUcZCIEW2Q-2BexpRIFr0-2BQIL-2F2DwZdKGdG-2BWrRWDGdQ02hc8kOHeUV3tcZAUT2VetzA-2FffBb-2FUBLTRgrrPUUfTfHnRLTl9O0RqlmQYAraG5eb-2BfmK8izuvJX9-2BaNHHlu1DqzFz07zf5aMhkjihlhkU0pofQq6rTNuy-2FF15ReKnODjLJ9q5vw-3D) scored every Wyoming legislator on a single question: how often do you actually vote the Republican platform? Ogden Driskill scored a 47%. A man who votes against his own party's platform more than half the time is not "merely right". He's a liberal hiding behind the "R" after his nameAnd the whole Establishment knows it. Americans for Prosperity, the big-money national outfit, is bankrolling more than a dozen candidates to knock off our people, Driskill included. Driskill told the Times how he feels in plain English:"I hate the Freedom Caucus and how they do business."Noted.Chip Neiman thought so little of the threat that he gave up the speaker's gavel to challenge Driskill head-on, and it all comes down to next Tuesday. Even the columnists see it. Dave Simpson has written for the Cowboy State Daily for 39 years, he is not a caucus member, and he warned his readers that if they toss Chip and the Wyoming Freedom Caucus members out, "we will deserve the bluer, more liberal state we become."As caucus chairwoman Rachel Williams puts it, the caucus's supporters are the silent majority. August 18 is the day for them to be heard.

**RADIO CLIP OF THE WEEK** This one will spike your blood pressure. **West Virginia Freedom Caucus** **Chairman Chris Anders** has spent two years pushing one simple idea: if the government wants to track everywhere your car goes with those Flock surveillance cameras, it should have to get a warrant first. Two years running he has introduced the bill. Two years running it has gone nowhere. The man it keeps dying in front of is Judiciary Chairman JB Akers, who told the press that Anders "submits sloppily drafted bills given to him by outside groups."Take a listen...and then ask Chairman Akers exactly which part of the Fourth Amendment he finds so poorly written.

# 107,931 Marylanders Have Left Maryland Under Wes Moore.
_"You brought your game today, Mr. Cox." - state leader at MACo_

Dear friend,
I just stepped off the stage from my first candidate forum with Gov. Moore. We crushed it. But before I tell you about that, we have an urgent deadline. [I have only 72 hours to raise the funds for our first financial report](https://us.list-manage.com/lptbN6_fUn8?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) to show we have enough to fight to win against the governor who has given us one of the highest taxed states in the nation, worst schools (38th), worst economy (2nd to last), and highest electric bills - all while traveling the nation running for high office.

Could you stop what you are doing and donate the maximum you are able to right now to help us post the strongest financial report yet? It will show the world that Maryland wants "No Moore!".

Gov. Moore and I just today had our first forum before the Maryland Association of Counties (MACo) where we were asked to give our vision and answer questions concerning the economy and cost-shifting to the Counties. Watch my speech [here](https://us.list-manage.com/fFIQokGiVvW?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) or at the above link - we are on fire and ready to serve and turn our beautiful state around.

Only 72 hours to help us with this urgent report deadline. Thank you for helping with any amount!

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Maryland Governor

Fellow Patriot,

I want to remind you a little about who I am and why I am running.

I grew up in the Hudson Valley. My parents dedicated their lives to this community, my mother as a teacher and my father as a local business owner. They taught me early what matters: hard work, personal responsibility, and pride in where you come from. _Those are Hudson Valley values. Those are American values._

**And they are nothing like what I am watching spread across this country right now.**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Open your banking app. Go to settings. Hey folks,
This one is personal.
A New York Times story just dropped detailing how the Trump administration has been targeting my company--and I sat down with [Adam Mockler](https://open.substack.com/users/72893096-adam-mockler?utm_source=mentions) to talk about what that actually looks like when you're living through it. The legal bills. The threats. The toll on my family and my team. And why I refuse to let any of it scare me into silence.
Here are a few moments you don't want to miss:
* [**00:01:58**] I break down how this started, from a conspiracy theory and a House Judiciary Committee subpoena to an ongoing fight involving Trump's DOJ.
* [**00:05:11**] Why I decided that if they were going to drag me into this fight, I was going to speak out--and why I see this as part of a much bigger pattern.
* [**00:09:05**] The part people don't see: six-figure legal costs, endless calls with lawyers, disruption to my business, and the mental toll that comes with it.
* [**00:14:39**] We get into the broader strategy behind Trump's politics: convincing Americans that everyone and everything is corrupt so his own abuses start to feel normal.
* [**00:19:37**] Why independent media matters so much right now--and why attempts to intimidate people speaking out can end up making all of us stronger.

This conversation is bigger than what's happening to me. It's about what happens when political power is used to intimidate critics, what fear does to people and institutions, and why we need independent voices willing to keep showing up anyway. **We also talk about corruption, accountability, the changing media landscape, and the kind of democracy we 're trying to build together. subject: What is YOUR top issue?
body:
Take my quick survey and tell me what we must address first.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Yu4x9BmAgkE?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,
I’m going to be honest: politicians spend a lot of time telling people what they should care about.
_I would rather listen._
As one of the first members of our campaign, your opinion matters to me. I want to know which issue is most important to you and your family right now.
Will you take my quick TOP ISSUE SURVEY?
---
| [TAKE THE TOP ISSUE SURVEY >> ](https://us.list-manage.com/SM0i10UfQ3q?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
**What issue matters most?**
* Lowering the cost of groceries, gas, housing, and childcare
* Creating good-paying jobs and strengthening our local economy
* Cutting taxes, wasteful spending, and government red tape
* Backing law enforcement and keeping our communities safe
* Protecting family farms and strengthening American agriculture
* Making healthcare and prescription drugs more affordable
* Empowering parents and expanding workforce and trade education
* Securing America and restoring trust in government

_Or is there another issue that matters to you most?_

It will only take a minute to weigh in, but your answer will help shape the priorities and message of this campaign.
[**SHARE MY TOP ISSUE >> **](https://us.list-manage.com/Bm8IYi6kJzu?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Central New Yorkers deserve a representative who hears them, respects them, and fights for them. That starts with listening to you.
Thank you for being part of this team.
Kailee Buller
[**P.S. I will be reviewing these responses personally. Please submit yours today!**](https://us.list-manage.com/dRqzT_VxsZl?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

The Trumps (and their MAGA friends) are using the office of the Presidency to enrich themselves in a way we have never, ever seen in American history.
